Its proximity to the Persian Gulf also provides comparatively secure access to oil and gas, giving it resources that many rival economies lack. As China's relative decline continues, India could attract a substantial share of manufacturing capacity now moving away from Chinese supply chains. Furthermore, should China and Russia experience serious instability, India would be well placed to exert considerable influence across the Eurasian continental landmass. The claim is obviously bullish, but the underlying strategic advantages are difficult to dismiss.
clips.source_hint: An optimistic post argues that India could become a superpower by 2030.

clips.text_zh: 「點解fat people以為食肉健康？」帖主話，Annals of Internal Medicine一系列研究發現，少食紅肉同加工肉，同較低總死亡率、較低心血管病死亡率有統計顯著關係。靠戒maintenance唔係ego，係body check。
clips.text_en_b1: Why do fat people think meat is healthy when the science shows it is unhealthy? The post says studies in the Annals of Internal Medicine found significantly lower total and cardiovascular mortality among people eating less red and processed meat. Fat people being angry about this is predictable, but the evidence still matters.
clips.text_en_b2: “Why do fat people think eating meat is healthy?” The post points to a series of studies in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which found statistically significant associations between eating less red and processed meat and lower overall mortality, including cardiovascular deaths. Although people may dislike being challenged, dismissing the evidence because it questions their identity does not change the findings. Cutting back for maintenance is not about ego; it is simply paying attention to what the body needs.
clips.text_en_c1: 'Why do fat people think eating meat is healthy when the science shows the opposite?' The post cites a series of studies published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which found statistically significant associations between eating less red and processed meat and lower overall mortality, including reduced cardiovascular mortality. Whether anyone finds this conclusion unwelcome is largely beside the point. Maintaining personal health is not an exercise in ego, however uncomfortable the evidence may be; it is a routine check on what the body is telling us. The findings warrant attention rather than reflexive denial.
clips.text_en_c2: “Why do fat people think eating meat is healthy?” The poster points to a series of studies published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which found that lower consumption of red and processed meat was statistically associated with lower overall mortality and cardiovascular mortality. The implication is stark: reducing meat is not merely an exercise in maintaining one's physique or appeasing an inflated ego, but a legitimate health precaution grounded in epidemiological evidence. People who feel personally challenged by the findings may respond with predictable anger, yet emotional discomfort does not alter the data. If diet influences long-term mortality, defending an unhealthy pattern on personal grounds is an extraordinarily weak argument.
clips.source_hint: A fitness thread attacks the idea that red meat is healthy and cites mortality studies.

clips.text_en_c2: Every anonymous poster on /biz/ fancies himself the next Michael Burry after watching a 17-minute YouTube video on credit spreads. He draws a red triangle on TradingView, announces with theatrical certainty that “THE EVERYTHING BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO POP,” and treats a chart resembling a bearish flag as financial insight. His forecasting record is, to put it generously, unconventional: he has supposedly predicted 38 of the last two recessions, an achievement that neatly demonstrates the difficulty of calling a collapse before it occurs. Meanwhile, the S&P fell by 0.4% on Friday, presumably far less dramatic than his imminent apocalypse. Confidence, in this forum, remains comfortably detached from calibration.
clips.source_hint: The post mocks amateur market doomsters who call every bubble the next big collapse.

clips.text_zh: 我喺2024年11月高位將全副身家套入 MSTR。兩年慢慢流乾晒成個net worth。每次細細 pump 都畀我啲希望，翌日又 dump。每次「averaged down」，實際只跌得更慘。我只想攞返啲錢，連 MSTR 帶住 BTC 都跌咗，我真係唔知點算。

clips.text_en_c2: In November 2024, at the height of the mania, I aped my entire life savings into MSTR. clips.text_en_b1: Can you actually make money from forex trading, or is it mostly a meme? Some people treat charts and online signals like real expertise. For me, CFD losses already feel expensive enough. It would be good to hear from anyone with a realistic, repeatable approach.
clips.text_en_b2: So, a genuine question: can you actually make money trading forex, or is it largely a meme? It looks like an incredibly difficult path, especially when people treat chart patterns and online signals as genuine expertise. For me, blowing money on CFDs already feels like paying tuition for a very expensive lesson. It would be reassuring to hear from anyone with a realistic, repeatable approach that produces normal returns instead of fantasy screenshots.
clips.text_en_c1: Can people realistically make money from forex trading, or is the whole thing largely a meme? The charts and online signals that circulate often masquerade as genuine expertise, although the path to consistent returns appears extremely difficult. My own losses through CFDs already feel like an exorbitant tuition fee. If anyone has a realistic, repeatable approach that does not depend on hindsight or luck, I would be interested to hear it.
clips.text_en_c2: Can one actually make money trading forex, or is the entire enterprise a elaborate meme dressed up in technical jargon? Charts, candlesticks and signal groups are routinely treated as expertise, although most participants would struggle to define risk management without resorting to platitudes. Having already paid for my education in life lessons through CFD losses, I am not eager to repeat the experiment. What I would welcome is an account from someone who has achieved consistent, repeatable returns, preferably one that acknowledges the long road, the drawdowns and the unglamorous arithmetic involved. Otherwise, the honest conclusion may be that this is a casino with extra steps.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ thread asks whether forex trading is profitable or merely a meme.

Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney also backed a public letter demanding his return. clips.text_en_b1: Teslas are the best. I cannot believe people still buy Big Three cars that are basically twentieth-century technology. I have never been so happy with a car as I am with my Tesla. Its acceleration is unreal for the price. It is also much more convenient without waiting for gas.

clips.text_en_c2: Teslas are, quite simply, the best cars on the road. I have never been happier with a car than I am with my Tesla, and I say that as someone who long suspected enthusiasm was clouding my judgement. The acceleration is frankly absurd for the price, delivering performance that would have seemed implausible a generation earlier, and the ownership experience is underscored by convenience. There is no queueing at a petrol station, no fumbling for a nozzle, no lingering in the forecourt; the whole errand is reduced to arriving and leaving.

Instead of squatting, she performs something that looks remarkably like a deadlift. It is strange, because she seems powerful and strong, yet her knees and hips hardly move in a way that resembles proper technique. clips.text_en_c1: At the gym today, I ran into the girl I used to talk to at university. She is tall and broad-shouldered, and she wants a six-pack, but her squat form is terrible. Rather than squatting, she appears to be performing repeated deadlifts, with neither her knees nor her hips moving as they should. clips.text_en_c2: At the gym today, I caught sight of the girl I used to chat with at university, and she has undeniably filled out: tall, broad-shouldered, and evidently determined to carve out a six-pack. Unfortunately, her squat technique is abysmal, since she performs the movement as though it were a deadlift, driving her hips too far back and loading the knees in a way that bears little resemblance to competent form. It was painful to witness, particularly given how much mass she is moving. A trainer should intervene before she subjects her knees and lower back to unnecessary strain, though I confess I found it difficult not to keep watching, since today was chiefly leg day.

clips.text_en_b1: I aped my life savings into MSTR at the top in November 2024. For two years, my net worth slowly bled out. Every little pump gave me hope, but it dumped the next day. Averaging down only made things worse. I am down $70,000, and I may never financially recover. No clear setup here, just pain.
clips.text_en_b2: “I threw my entire life savings into MSTR at the top in November 2024.” For two years, my net worth slowly bled out. Every minor pump gave me a flicker of hope, yet it dumped again the following day. Averaging down only deepened the damage. I’m currently down $70,000, and honestly, I may never financially recover from this. There was no clear setup here — only pain, and a lesson I paid for the hard way.
clips.text_en_c1: In November 2024, I aped my entire life savings into MSTR at the top, a decision whose stupidity becomes clearer with every passing month. For two years, my net worth has slowly bled out; each minor pump revived my hopes, only for the stock to dump again the following day. Averaging down merely increased the size of the mistake. I am now down $70,000 and may never recover financially. If there is no credible setup, the sensible response is to watch from the sidelines, not to go all in.
clips.text_en_c2: In November 2024, at the height of the frenzy, I aped my entire life savings into MSTR. What followed was not a clean collapse but two years of slow financial bleeding, with every modest pump reviving hope just long enough for the stock to dump again the following day. Averaging down only deepened the wound. I am currently $70,000 lighter and may never recover financially. There was no convincing setup here, merely conviction without discipline. In hindsight, observation would have been wiser than putting everything on one disastrous position.
clips.source_hint: An anon describes major MSTR losses and repeated averaging down.

clips.text_zh: 香港細地最怕唔係負荷計錯，係地下管線同排水搞清楚就要拆晒成個假設。斜坡調查要睇GI report、soil nailing同factor of safety；混凝土同鋼都要跟load path。Beam同column唔係畫完就算，現場施工先知個method係咪work，靠AI續命都救唔到一次site mistake。
clips.text_en_b1: Today was a slope investigation and condition survey day. I checked GI reports, soil nailing details, drainage, underground utilities, and factor of safety. Then I followed the structural load path from beams to columns, including concrete and steel. Every method needs a proper check on site. AI can help with the reports, but it cannot replace engineering judgment.
clips.text_en_b2: Today was a day spent on slope investigation and a condition survey. I reviewed GI reports, soil nailing details, drainage, underground utilities, and the factor of safety, then traced the structural load path from beams through columns, covering both concrete and steel. What matters most on these small Hong Kong sites is getting the assumptions right before anything gets built. No method is proven until it survives site conditions, and AI can’t rescue a single engineering mistake.
clips.text_en_c1: Today involved a slope investigation and condition survey, where the critical difficulty often lies not in a miscalculated load, but in unresolved assumptions concerning underground utilities and drainage. I reviewed the GI reports, soil-nailing details, and factor of safety, then traced the structural load path from beams through columns, covering both concrete and steel. A method cannot be considered workable merely because it appears sound on paper; it must be checked against actual site conditions. AI may streamline the reports, but no algorithm can repair a single site mistake or replace sound engineering judgment.
clips.text_en_c2: Today involved a slope investigation and structural condition survey, where the most treacherous pitfalls rarely concern a miscalculated load; they concern the assumptions embedded in drainage, underground utilities, and the interaction between them. Reviewing the GI report, soil-nailing details, and factor of safety meant following the structural load path through both concrete and steel, from beams to columns and ultimately into the foundations. A method may look impeccable on paper, but the site has the final say. AI can streamline documentation, yet it cannot compensate for flawed engineering judgment or a single consequential mistake on site.
clips.source_hint: A geopolitical post used here as a prompt for Hong Kong civil and structural site work.

clips.text_zh: 開源code俾AI學完，再出嚟同原本developer競爭，條GPL真係寫得幾清楚。你哋成日問AI會唔會取代工程師？睇下Nvidia同model training嗰班人，AI連自己都未settle落嚟，邊隻會先replace site work？呢個先係重點。
clips.text_en_b1: Open-source versus AI. Current AI models were trained on huge amounts of internet data without permission from everyone. The GNU GPL says that projects using covered code must publish their entire project under the same license. Other licenses include MIT. The argument is simple: developers built the code, but AI companies used it without permission.
clips.text_en_b2: Open-source code versus AI. Today’s models were trained on enormous amounts of internet data without permission from the people who wrote it. The GNU GPL is fairly clear: if your project incorporates covered code, you must publish the entire project under the same license, whereas MIT offers more flexibility. The core argument is straightforward. Developers built the code, and AI companies used it anyway. Before asking whether AI will replace engineers, look at how unsettled the field already is.
clips.text_en_c1: Open-source code versus AI is not a hypothetical dispute: developers created the code, while AI companies trained their models on vast quantities of internet data, including protected material, without obtaining permission from every contributor. The GNU GPL is reasonably explicit that a project incorporating covered code must publish its entire project under the same licence, although alternatives such as MIT permit more permissive use. This is precisely why claims that AI will replace engineers deserve scepticism. Before replacing site work, the technology still needs to establish that it can reliably handle the work developers already do.
clips.text_en_c2: The tension between open-source software and AI is more straightforward than either side would prefer. Developers publish code so that others may study, modify, and redistribute it; AI companies then train models on vast quantities of that material, often without the consent of everyone who created it. The GNU GPL is unambiguous: a project incorporating covered code must distribute the entire project under the same licence, although alternatives such as MIT permit more permissive use. The underlying grievance is equally plain: developers built the code, while AI firms appropriated its value. Consider Nvidia and model training before assuming the technology has already replaced engineers.
clips.source_hint: A discussion about open-source licenses and AI training on internet data.

clips.text_zh: Starship又一次成功，Elon照例贏。香港新聞成日放大火箭新聞，但低智商poster最鍾意寫「Destroyed」。不過要問清楚今次到底有咩historic：係第十次catch定係其他突破？有data先可以判斷，唔係每次升空都值得當成大事。
clips.text_en_b1: Starship success. Elon wins again, baby. Doubters with low IQ were completely destroyed. But what exactly was historic about what SpaceX just did? This was like rocket number ten they caught. I thought the hype would be over by now. The technical achievement matters more than repeating the same slogan.
clips.text_en_b2: Starship succeeded again, so Elon wins once more, baby. Hong Kong news outlets keep amplifying rocket stories, while low-IQ posters insist on writing “destroyed” in every thread. Still, it’s worth asking what was actually historic here. Was this their tenth booster catch, or some other genuine breakthrough? You need data before you can judge, because not every launch deserves to be treated as a major milestone. The technical achievement matters more than the slogan.
clips.text_en_c1: Starship has succeeded again, and Elon wins, as usual. Hong Kong news outlets routinely inflate every rocket development, while the least intellectually rigorous posters continue to proclaim that the doubters were “destroyed.” The more pertinent question, however, is what exactly SpaceX achieved that was genuinely historic. Was this its tenth successful catch, or did the flight involve some other breakthrough? Claims require data, and not every launch deserves to be treated as a major milestone simply because the familiar slogan has been repeated.
clips.text_en_c2: Starship has succeeded again, and Elon, as ever, emerges the ostensible victor. Hong Kong news outlets amplify rocket developments almost by reflex, while low-IQN posters habitually announce that the doubters have been comprehensively destroyed. The more useful question, however, is what precisely was historic about SpaceX’s latest achievement: was this merely the tenth vehicle caught, or did it represent some other meaningful advance? Genuine assessment requires data and an exact account of what occurred. Not every launch warrants elevation into a landmark, and the technical achievement matters more than recycling the same triumphant slogan.
clips.source_hint: A celebratory post about SpaceX, Starship, and Elon Musk.

clips.text_zh: 今日個gym thread有人話揀隻CD，lifts即刻多5磅。靠AI續命咁耐，終於有啲quantified result。肥仔信如果聽到呢段一定話得5磅太少，但我哋這些廢柴照樣舉鐵，form差都照練。Music係儀式感，5磅先係bonus。
clips.text_en_b1: How important is music in the gym? If you pick any CD from this display, your lifts will go up by at least 5 pounds. That is the thread's rule. The advice is probably nonsense, but music can still help you get through warm-ups and heavy sets. Good training habits matter more than any magical playlist.
clips.text_en_b2: How important is music when you’re lifting? According to this thread, pick any CD from the display and your lifts will jump by at least five pounds. The advice is probably nonsense, but there’s something to it: music can carry you through warm-ups and heavy sets when motivation starts to fade. Although most of us are pretty useless, we still train even when our form is terrible. Music is the ritual, and five pounds is just a bonus.
clips.text_en_c1: How important is music when you train? The gym thread’s rule was that selecting any CD from the display would increase your lifts by at least five pounds. This is, of course, probably nonsense, yet the quantified result is no less amusing for being implausible. A larger man would undoubtedly argue that five pounds is negligible; the rest of us would continue lifting despite questionable form. Music provides ritual, atmosphere, and a psychological push through warm-ups and heavy sets. Any measurable improvement is a bonus, but consistent training habits matter far more than a magical playlist.
clips.text_en_c2: Today’s gym thread offered a characteristically dubious proposition: choose any CD from the display, and your lifts will increase by at least five pounds. Apparently, this is the thread’s official rule, although no credible hypertrophy mechanism has yet been identified. Nevertheless, the advice may possess some practical value, since music can carry you through warm-ups, blunt fatigue during demanding sets, and the final repetitions that might otherwise disappear. Every self-proclaimed macho lifter will insist that five pounds is a negligible bonus, yet the rest of us continue training regardless, often with imperfect form. Music supplies the ritual; the extra weight remains, at most, a cheerful embellishment.
clips.source_hint: A fitness thread jokes that music from a CD display adds five pounds to every lift.

clips.text_zh: AotS同AotY今季真係唔會好返。多謝anons仍然捧場傾favorite，仲有blind girl anime同Futsutsuka Akujo入honourable mentions。Demon Slayer同 Gundam 00至少仲有得追，但AOT而家個勁抽離，睇完只係想即刻開Structures嗰條片返工。
clips.text_en_b1: Attack on Titan season four will not get any better. What were your favorites this year? Honorable mentions go to the blind girl anime and Futsutsuka Akujo. The season has already disappointed me, but I still want to hear about the best moments. Some shows disappear from memory, while others stay with you.
clips.text_en_b2: Attack on Titan season four isn’t going to get any better, although I’d still love to hear which moments you all considered the strongest this year. Honorable mentions go to the blind girl anime and Futsutsuka Akujo. Demon Slayer and Gundam 00 are at least still worth following, but AOT’s momentum has completely collapsed. Some shows fade into memory, while others stick around, and after finishing this season, I just want to open up Structures and get back to work.
clips.text_en_c1: Attack on Titan season four is unlikely to improve, and the series will probably not recover its former strength this season. Nevertheless, I would still like to hear which anime people considered the best, along with their favourite moments. Honorable mentions go to the blind girl anime and Futsutsuka Akujo, while Demon Slayer and Gundam 00 at least remain worth following. AOT’s momentum has now drained away, leaving me inclined to watch that Structures video about working immediately after finishing the episode.
clips.text_en_c2: Attack on Titan’s fourth season is unlikely to improve, and AOTY will fare no better. Nevertheless, thanks to the anons still turning up to discuss their favourites, the blind girl anime and Futsutsuka Akujo deserve honourable mentions. Demon Slayer and Gundam 00 remain watchable, even if they cannot entirely compensate for AOT’s present trajectory. The season has already disappointed me sufficiently that finishing it leaves me with an immediate urge to watch the Structures video and return to work. Some anime fade from memory as though they never existed; others remain lodged there permanently, however reluctantly.
clips.source_hint: An anime thread asks for Attack on Titan favorites and mentions two other series.

clips.text_zh: Bitcoin依家係超賣。廢柴今日平咗short。睇落應該有個relief rally。等升返去先再算。75k就會再short。呢鋪又係 tuition，thx。
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin is oversold, so I closed my short today. No matter how I measure it, Bitcoin is due for a relief rally. I will enter another short at 75k. Thank you for your attention to this PSA.
clips.text_en_b2: Bitcoin is clearly oversold, so I closed my short position today. However I measure it, the setup seems due for a relief rally, although I do not expect it to last forever. I will wait for the price to recover before entering another short at 75k. This trade is tuition again, but at least I am learning. Thank you for your attention to this PSA.
clips.text_en_c1: Bitcoin is currently oversold, so I closed my short position today. Regardless of which indicator I use, the charts suggest that a relief rally is overdue; however, I will wait for the rebound before deciding what to do next. If the price climbs to $75,000, I will enter another short there. I have been burned by this trade before, but it is tuition nonetheless. Thank you for reading this public service announcement.
clips.text_en_c2: Bitcoin is decisively oversold, so I closed my short position today. Whatever metric one uses—momentum, mean reversion, or simply the severity of the recent decline—the setup appears ripe for a relief rally. I have no intention of pretending this constitutes a durable trend reversal; I merely intend to wait for the rebound, reassess conditions, and then re-enter a short at $75,000. It is another round of tuition, paid in the currency everyone seems to enjoy losing. Thank you for your attention to this public service announcement.
clips.source_hint: The OP closes a Bitcoin short and plans to re-enter at 75K.

clips.text_zh: 我終於recognize個現實：crypto死咗。一直做100% ETH baggie，完全married to my bags，靠住一堆「ETH去10k」嘅廢故事撐住。最近幾個星期，我發現根本冇可能。冇tokenization，冇新資金入嚟。Ethereum乜都唔做，就係一班assholes聞自己嘅屁。
clips.text_en_b1: I finally realized that crypto is dead. I have been a 100% ETH bagholder for so long, completely married to my bags and believing silly narratives about ETH reaching $10K. No tokenization, no more money coming in. Ethereum does nothing. It is a science project made by a group of assholes sniffing their own farts.
clips.text_en_b2: I have finally admitted the painful reality: crypto is dead. For years I remained a 100 percent ETH bagholder, completely married to my bags and obsessed with silly narratives about ETH reaching 10k. However, nothing is tokenized and no fresh capital is entering the market. Ethereum does nothing; it is a science project built by a group of assholes sniffing their own farts.
clips.text_en_c1: I finally have to admit that crypto is dead. I have spent years as a 100 percent ETH bagholder, effectively married to my position while relying on increasingly absurd narratives that ETH would reach $10,000. The past few weeks have made the conclusion unavoidable: there is no meaningful tokenization, nor any new capital entering the ecosystem. Ethereum appears to accomplish nothing beyond sustaining a group of assholes who keep sniffing their own farts and calling it progress.
clips.text_en_c2: I have finally confronted an uncomfortable truth: crypto is dead, at least in the form I chose to marry. For years, I remained a 100% ETH bagholder, wholly committed to my position and sustained by hollow narratives predicting that ETH would reach $10,000. Recent weeks have made the arithmetic impossible to ignore. There is no meaningful tokenization, nor any fresh capital entering the ecosystem. Ethereum accomplishes nothing; it is a science project devised by a group of assholes who appear to be sniffing their own farts.
clips.source_hint: The OP rejects Ethereum's old narratives after holding ETH for years.

clips.text_zh: 今日返site做slope investigation，睇soil nailing同GI report。成條load path要由failure plane、soil nail、drainage一路check到retaining structure。Beam同column就照load path逐個load take，唔可以靠feel。考牌都未完，靠AI續命。
clips.text_en_b1: Today I checked a slope investigation, a GI report, soil nailing, drainage, and underground utilities. The load path must connect the failure plane to each nail and the retaining structure. Structural design works the same way: trace every load through the beams and columns, then check each step.
clips.text_en_b2: Today I went back to the site to review the slope investigation, the GI report, soil nailing, drainage, and underground utilities. The entire load path has to be traced from the failure plane through every soil nail and drainage element to the retaining structure. Structural design follows the same principle: follow each load through the beams and columns and check every step, rather than relying on intuition. I am still studying for my license.
clips.text_en_c1: Today I returned to the site to review the slope investigation, focusing on the geotechnical investigation report, soil nailing, and drainage details. The entire load path has to be followed from the potential failure plane, through each soil nail and drainage system, and on to the retaining structure. Structural calculations follow the same principle: every load must be traced through the beams and columns, with each transfer checked rather than guessed from intuition. My exams are not finished, so AI is keeping me alive.
clips.text_en_c2: Today I returned to the site to inspect the slope investigation, reviewing the geotechnical report, soil nailing, drainage arrangements, and underground utilities. The entire load path must be traced coherently from the potential failure plane through each soil nail and drainage element to the retaining structure. Structural design follows essentially the same principle: follow every load sequentially through the beams and columns, verify each transfer, and never substitute instinct for calculation. My professional qualification is still incomplete, so AI is currently keeping the whole operation marginally alive.
clips.source_hint: This engineering-themed thread fits a civil and structural engineering discussion.

clips.text_zh: NVIDIA員工要求Jensen Huang返嚟做big boss。有人話：「如果你相信mission，就帶THE boss返嚟。」員工唔係為份工做，係因為想跟住佢。AI hardware仲係我份工最大嘅威脅，特別係連Civil都要靠software嗰部分。
clips.text_en_b1: NVIDIA employees demand that Jensen Huang be reinstated as the big boss. One employee wrote, “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss.” The post claims 80% of employees are millionaires and NVIDIA has the industry's lowest turnover.
clips.text_en_b2: NVIDIA employees are demanding that Jensen Huang return as the big boss. One employee put it directly: “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss.” People are not working there merely for the salary; many want to follow Huang again. AI hardware remains the greatest threat to my job, particularly the software-dependent part, including even civil engineering. The post claims that 80 percent of employees are millionaires and that NVIDIA has the industry’s lowest turnover.
clips.text_en_c1: NVIDIA employees are demanding that Jensen Huang return as the big boss. One employee put it succinctly: “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss.” The argument is not merely about compensation or job security; people want to follow Huang because of the culture and direction he created. Meanwhile, AI hardware remains the greatest threat to my own job, particularly in fields such as civil engineering, where an increasing share of the work already depends on software rather than conventional technical expertise.
clips.text_en_c2: NVIDIA employees are demanding that Jensen Huang return as the unequivocal big boss. One employee put it succinctly: “If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss.” The post argues that staff are not merely employed by the company but fundamentally motivated by working under Huang. It also claims that 80% of employees are millionaires and that NVIDIA maintains the industry's lowest employee turnover. AI hardware remains the greatest competitive threat to my livelihood, particularly the software-defined segment now penetrating even civil engineering.
clips.source_hint: The post focuses on Nvidia staff demanding Jensen Huang's return.

clips.text_zh: SpaceX rocket又爆炸。成個nationwide flight shutdown都停咗先搞呢個？你哋之前吹得咁神，engineering failure照樣照炸。香港細到地鐵一鑽就爆，其他地方根本冇live room。
clips.text_en_b1: SpaceX rocket explodes. They staged a nationwide flight shutdown for this? After all the hype, an engineering failure still ends with an explosion. It makes me appreciate the scale difference: Hong Kong is crowded, but America has much more space.
clips.text_en_b2: A SpaceX rocket has exploded again, and they staged a nationwide flight shutdown just to handle it. After all the hype, an engineering failure still results in an explosion, which makes the company’s previous boasting look rather ridiculous. It also highlights the scale difference between the two countries: Hong Kong is so crowded that one subway tunnel could cause chaos, while America has far more space. Elsewhere, there was not even a live room.
clips.text_en_c1: A SpaceX rocket has exploded again. Did the company really suspend flights nationwide merely to deal with this? After generating so much hype, the company still managed to turn an engineering failure into another explosion. Watching the footage, I was struck by the scale of the differences between the two countries. Hong Kong is so densely populated that one钻孔 can apparently cause chaos, whereas America has far more space and consequently fewer immediate consequences when something goes wrong in the sky.
clips.text_en_c2: A SpaceX rocket has exploded, and the spectacle apparently warranted grounding the entire nationwide flight network while officials dealt with the incident. After so much corporate hype and technological self-congratulation, the outcome remains stubbornly unchanged: an engineering failure culminates in an explosion. There is something clarifying about scale, although not necessarily comforting. Hong Kong is so densely packed that a subway tunnel piercing the ground can trigger chaos, whereas America possesses far more room to absorb such failures, both geographically and operationally, without every disruption becoming a national emergency.
clips.source_hint: The OP questions SpaceX's rocket test and nationwide flight shutdown.

clips.text_zh: 2023年turn 30嗰陣成個人生crisis。冇變高，但至少唔再做fatass。之後做咗一年weight loss，再做兩年lifting，目標係加返leam muscle mass。2026年望住鏡唔frown，今日覺得自己made it。肥仔信見到我呢身可能又話：咁瘦做乜啫。
clips.text_en_b1: I turned 30 in 2023 and had a crisis. I could not change my height, but I stopped being a fatass. I started a one-year weight-loss journey, then spent two years lifting to gain lean muscle mass. In 2026, I looked in the mirror and finally did not frown.
clips.text_en_b2: When I turned 30 in 2023, my life entered a crisis because I could not change my height, but I could at least stop being a fatass. I then spent one year losing weight and another two years lifting, with the aim of rebuilding lean muscle mass. By 2026, I could look in the mirror without frowning and finally feel that I had made it. Some bigger guys may see my thinner body and wonder why I bothered.
clips.text_en_c1: When I turned 30 in 2023, my life entered an identity crisis. I could not change my height, but at least I could stop being a fatass. I spent one year losing weight and then another two lifting weights, with the aim of rebuilding myself as someone with more lean muscle mass. In 2026, I looked in the mirror and finally did not frown. I feel as though I have made it, although the chubby guy who sees my current physique may still wonder why I have become so thin.
clips.text_en_c2: When I turned 30 in 2023, I experienced a full-blown crisis of identity. I could not alter my height, but I could at least stop being a fatass. I devoted one year to losing weight and then spent two years lifting, with the explicit aim of rebuilding a lean, functional musculature rather than merely attaining a smaller number on the scale. In 2026, I looked in the mirror without frowning and felt, for perhaps the first time in years, that I had made it. Other people, particularly those who consider fatness a moral failing, may accuse me of now being too thin; nevertheless, I have no intention of returning to what I was.
clips.source_hint: The OP describes turning 30, losing weight, and building lean muscle.

clips.text_zh: Zeke嘅euthanasia plan成功，Eren嘅genocide plan又成功。最後human死咗80%，Eldians冇晒power of titan shifting，全世界更加恨佢哋。到底係Isayama被逼寫成咁，或者AoT一開始就係壞嘅？
clips.text_en_b1: Zeke's euthanasia plan works. Eren's genocide plan works too. Yet 80% of humanity is wiped out, the Eldians lose the power of Titan shifting, and the world hates them even more. Was Isayama forced to write this ending, or was Attack on Titan bad from the start?
clips.text_en_b2: Zeke’s euthanasia plan succeeded, while Eren’s genocide plan succeeded as well, although neither outcome brought anything positive. In the end, 80 percent of humanity was wiped out, the Eldians lost their power of Titan shifting, and the rest of the world hated them even more. This raises an uncomfortable question: was Isayama forced to write such a conclusion, or had Attack on Titan been fundamentally flawed from the very beginning?
clips.text_en_c1: Zeke’s euthanasia plan succeeds, and Eren’s genocide plan succeeds as well, although the consequences are catastrophic. Eighty percent of humanity is wiped out, the Eldians are stripped of their ability to inherit the power of the Titan shifters, and the rest of the world emerges with even stronger hatred toward them. The ending therefore appears to satisfy both competing objectives while destroying almost everything either side wanted. Was Isayama forced into this conclusion, or had Attack on Titan been fundamentally broken from its very beginning?
clips.text_en_c2: Zeke's euthanasia plan succeeds, and Eren's plan for the eradication of humanity succeeds alongside it. Yet the consequences are bleak: 80% of the global population is annihilated, the Eldians are stripped of their ability to inherit the power of the Titans, and the surviving world regards them with even greater hatred than before. The ending invites an uncomfortable question about authorship and structural inevitability. Was Hajime Isayama constrained by circumstances, circumstances largely of his own construction, into writing such a conclusion? Or was Attack on Titan fundamentally broken from its inception?
clips.source_hint: The OP debates the ending and whether Attack on Titan was flawed from the start.

clips.text_zh: 我終於醒悟。Crypto死咗。一直做100% ETH baggie，同我啲「毒」結婚咗，落命喺「ETH去10K」呢啲傻逼敘事。依家冇tokenization，冇新錢流入乜都冇。Ethereum根本冇用，永遠唔會被採用。又係學費，但至少唔再問「ETH幾時返10K」。
clips.text_en_b1: I finally realized: crypto is dead. I've been a 100% ETH baggie for so long, completely married to my bags, believing in stupid made-up narratives that would send ETH to $10K. In the past couple of weeks, I realized it is never going to happen. No tokenization, no more money coming in, nothing. Ethereum does nothing.
clips.text_en_b2: I've finally come to my senses: crypto is dead. For years I was a 100% ETH bagholder, emotionally married to my bags and convinced by endless narratives that ETH would inevitably reach $10K. Over the past couple of weeks, I've accepted that this is never going to happen. There is no meaningful tokenization story, no fresh capital flowing in, and nothing left to justify the valuation. Ethereum does basically nothing, and it will never be adopted for anything serious.
clips.text_en_c1: I've finally come around to it: crypto is dead. For years I was a 100 percent ETH bagholder, thoroughly married to my position, and I believed every fabricated narrative that promised ETH would print $10K. Over the past couple of weeks, though, it has become painfully obvious that it is never going to happen. No tokenization story, no fresh inflows of capital, no catalyst whatsoever. Ethereum does nothing useful; it is a science project built by a roomful of assholes sniffing their own farts, and it will never be adopted for anything meaningful. Fine, tuition paid.
clips.text_en_c2: I have finally reached the point of clarity: crypto is dead. For years, I was a 100 percent ETH bagholder, emotionally married to my position and convinced that elaborate narratives about tokenization, adoption, and institutional money would eventually propel ETH to $10,000. In the past couple of weeks, however, the flow of new capital has dried up, and the promised use cases have failed to materialize. Ethereum, in practical terms, does almost nothing; it remains a sprawling science project built by people who appear to have mistaken their own fart jokes for a technological vision. Nothing will be adopted at scale. Perhaps I have merely paid an expensive tuition fee, but at least I no longer ask when ETH will return to $10,000.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post about abandoning Ethereum and its $10K dream.

clips.text_zh: 我做day trading第三日，而家整緊backtesting、forward testing同paper trading bot。我係咪傻，定其實做法啱？靠AI續命，個bot未ready已經先當transformation signal。
clips.text_en_b1: It's my third day learning day trading, and I'm making a backtesting, forward-testing, and paper-trading bot. Am I being retarded, or am I doing it right? This is what I saw on /biz/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: I'm on the third day of learning day trading, and somehow I've already started building a bot that handles backtesting, forward testing, and paper trading. Am I completely out of my mind, or is this actually the right way to approach it? These days you can lean on AI to keep the project alive, even before the bot is genuinely ready. It already treats something like a transformation signal, which feels slightly absurd.
clips.text_en_c1: Today marks my third day learning day trading, and I am currently assembling a bot that handles backtesting, forward testing, and paper trading. The question nagging at me is whether I am simply being retarded or whether, by some unlikely chance, I am doing this correctly. I am keeping the thing alive with AI assistance, because the bot is not even ready yet and I have already started treating every transformation signal as gospel. This is what /biz/ was discussing today, and I would genuinely appreciate someone telling me whether this is how it is supposed to work.
clips.text_en_c2: It is only my third day learning day trading, and I am already building a bot that conducts backtesting, forward testing, and paper trading. I am using AI to sustain the effort before the system is even remotely ready, while treating it as a transformation signal rather than a finished trading strategy. Am I being naive, or is this broadly the correct way to proceed? The process feels wildly accelerated, particularly because a functioning bot requires careful historical validation, realistic assumptions about execution, and safeguards against overfitting. Nevertheless, I am taking the first tentative steps, which is more than most beginners manage. This is what appeared on /biz/ today.
clips.source_hint: A beginner describes building a day-trading test bot.

clips.text_zh: Nvidia新CEO上任。Rajit Bhamra接任，做AI晶片王嘅工程主管。廢柴如我都要睇多兩眼：工程背景頂到最前，係咪代表NVIDIA由engineering-first行落去？AI接job嘅壓力又加多一層。
clips.text_en_b1: New CEO appointed. Nvidia Corp. appointed Rajit Bhamra as Chief Executive Officer, placing the veteran engineering leader in charge of the biggest company on Earth. Operating from the chipmaker's Santa Clara headquarters, he assumes command of the multi-trillion-dollar artificial intelligence giant whose processors and software platforms power the modern computing economy. He was born in a village in India.
clips.text_en_b2: Nvidia has appointed a new CEO: Rajit Bhamra, the veteran engineering executive who has spent years overseeing the company's AI chips. Even someone as hopeless as me has to take notice, because promoting the head of engineering to the top suggests NVIDIA may finally be shifting away from its engineering-first identity. At the same time, the pressure of competing for jobs against AI keeps growing. The company is enormous, but its strategy now seems tied tightly to one very narrow market.
clips.text_en_c1: New CEO appointed. Nvidia Corp. has named Rajit Bhamra Chief Executive Officer, putting the veteran engineering leader in charge of the biggest company on Earth. Operating out of the chipmaker's Santa Clara headquarters, he now assumes command of a multi-trillion-dollar artificial intelligence giant whose processors and software platforms power the modern computing economy. Even a useless dilettante like me has to take a second look at this: an engineering pedigree pushed to the very top of the organization, which raises the question of whether Nvidia is quietly moving away from its engineering-first identity. Whatever the case, the pressure on AI's new custodian has just increased by another layer.
clips.text_en_c2: Nvidia has appointed Rajit Bhamra as its new Chief Executive Officer, entrusting the veteran engineering leader with the responsibility of running what is now the world’s largest company by market value. Operating from Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters, he will oversee a multitrillion-dollar artificial-intelligence enterprise whose processors and software platforms underpin much of the modern computing economy. The appointment is significant because an engineer with decades of technical experience is taking charge at a moment when AI infrastructure has become strategically indispensable. Even someone as incurably mediocre as I am must take notice. Does his elevation signal that Nvidia remains engineering-first, or that the company is becoming a more conventional, commercially driven corporation? The pressure attached to the role is unquestionably immense.
clips.source_hint: A Bloomberg-based /biz/ post about Nvidia appointing Rajit Bhamra as CEO.

clips.text_zh: Jensen如果而家辭職，個名只剩「處理relationship問題走人嘅廢物」。留低，最多係一行footnote。佢就係NVIDIA，冇人替代到。走咗去玩golf？我諗AI empire仲需要工程腦，唔係只靠新聞稿。
clips.text_en_b1: He resigned. The retard should never have fallen for the pressure. Musk has 10 scandals a week and walks off scot-free every time. Nobody remembers them because his work overshadows them. If Jensen walks away now, he'll forever be known as the adulterer fuckup that walked away. If he stays, it'll be a footnote. He is the company. He made it.
clips.text_en_b2: He resigned, because the retard shouldn't have fallen for all that pressure in the first place. Musk gets away with ten scandals a week simply because his work overshadows every one of them. If Jensen walks away now, he'll be remembered forever as the adulterer fuckup who quit. If he stays, his tenure becomes a footnote at best. He is NVIDIA; nobody can replace him, because he built the company into what it is.
clips.text_en_c1: He resigned. The retard should never have succumbed to the pressure in the first place. Musk generates ten scandals a week and walks away scot-free every single time, because nobody remembers them; his work overshadows them all. If Jensen walks now, he will forever be remembered as the adulterer fuckup who walked away. If he stays, then he is a footnote at best. He is the company, and he made it. What the fuck is he going to do now, retire to a golf course? I remain convinced that the AI empire still needs an engineering brain in the room, not someone who lives off press releases.
clips.text_en_c2: Jensen Huang has resigned. He should never have yielded to the pressure in the first place. Musk produces ten scandals every week and strolls away without consequence, because his output eclipses the reputational wreckage. If Jensen walks away now, his legacy will crystallize as that of the adulterous executive who abandoned the company; if he stays, the whole episode may become no more than a footnote. He is Nvidia. He built the institution that bears his name, and nobody can genuinely replace him. His successors can issue polished statements, but they cannot replicate the engineering judgment, industry relationships, and institutional authority accumulated over decades. So what exactly is he going to do now? Play golf while the AI empire still requires a genuine engineering brain rather than press releases?
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread debating Jensen Huang leaving Nvidia.

clips.text_zh: Sony發明Blu-ray，collect licensing royalties 20年，專利到期收乾就announce exit。大家以為佢哋暗地研究200GB+ successor，結果入到R&D都冇乜。科技最怕唔做，唔係最怕失敗。靠AI續命靠晒。
clips.text_en_b1: Sony invents Blu-ray, collects licensing royalties for 20 years, then the patents expire and the royalties dry up. Sony announces its exit from Blu-ray production. Everyone assumes Sony was researching a successor, like a 200GB-plus optical disc. Then you look inside Sony's R&D: nothing now. When your $300 hard drive fails, you have another option. This came up on /g/ today.
clips.text_en_b2: Sony invented Blu-ray, collected licensing royalties for twenty years, and then, once the patents expired and the money dried up, announced its exit from production. Naturally, everyone assumed Sony had been quietly developing a successor, perhaps a 200GB-plus optical disc. But when you actually look inside Sony's R&D, there is essentially nothing. The terrifying part about technology isn't failure; it's simply doing nothing. Meanwhile, when your $300 hard drive dies, you have another option. This came up on /g/ today.
clips.text_en_c1: Sony invents Blu-ray, collects licensing royalties for twenty years, and then the patents expire and the royalties dry up, so Sony announces its exit from optical disc production. Everyone assumes that behind the curtain, Sony has been quietly researching a successor: some 200GB-plus optical format of our own. Then you peer inside Sony's R&D and find nothing whatsoever. Which is the real lesson here: technology dies from inaction far more often than from failure. When your $300 hard drive eventually fails, you will have no alternative at all. This came up on /g/ today, and the timing is not exactly flattering.
clips.text_en_c2: Sony invented Blu-ray, collected licensing royalties from it for two decades, and then announced its exit from optical-disc production as the relevant patents expired and the revenue stream dried up. Naturally, everyone assumed the company was secretly developing a successor capable of holding more than 200GB. Yet a glance inside Sony’s R&D effort reveals little more than inertia and empty promise. When a $300 hard drive finally fails, consumers will have no optical alternative worth mentioning. The deeper problem is not that Sony’s attempt failed, but that it stopped trying. Technological leadership is sustained by continued investment, not by commemorative slides about past achievements. This observation surfaced on /g/ today, and it is difficult to see where the next practical successor will come from.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ post about Sony leaving optical discs behind.

clips.text_zh: 點解大部分billionaires咁粗俗又冇想像力？以前有Howard Hughes，估係真係推動人類進步嗰種人。而家得Elon好似仲有試。幾百B USD拎出嚟，搞endowment、搞20年太空研究站、甚至免學費college都得。Money先，啲plan先係proof。
clips.text_en_b1: Why are most billionaires so crass and unimaginative? Where are the Howard Hughes and other industrialists pushing mankind forward? Elon is the only one who seems to try. For the hundreds of billions they throw around, they could create an endowment and a 20-year plan to build a mega research station in space, or build new colleges that research their interests with a fully tuition-free…
clips.text_en_b2: Why are so many billionaires crass, unimaginative, and obsessed with accumulating more money rather than pushing humanity forward? Where are the modern Howard Hugheses? Elon seems to be the only one still trying, because for the hundreds of billions they throw around, they could easily fund an endowment and a 20-year plan for a massive research station in space, or build entirely tuition-free colleges dedicated to their own interests. But they don't, which makes you wonder what happened to their ambition along the way.
clips.text_en_c1: Why are most billionaires so crass and unimaginative? Where have all the Howard Hughes figures gone, the industrialists who genuinely pushed mankind forward? Elon seems to be the only one still trying. For the hundreds of billions they throw around without much thought, they could establish an endowment and fund a twenty-year plan to build a mega research station in space, or endow new colleges that research their own interests with a fully tuition-free student body. Instead, they do none of it. Money first, and the plans come later, if they come at all. What exactly happened?
clips.text_en_c2: Why are so many billionaires vulgar, self-indulgent, and astonishingly unimaginative? Where are the modern equivalents of Howard Hughes and other industrialists who genuinely pushed civilization forward? Elon, at least, appears willing to try. Given the hundreds of billions of dollars they deploy so freely, billionaires could establish substantial endowments, commission a twenty-year programme to construct a major research station in space, or create new colleges devoted to their interests and offer them tuition-free. They rarely do. Instead, conspicuous consumption, private jets, and impulsive acquisition dominate the public imagination. Money, however, is not a plan; it merely supplies the raw material. The proof of ambition lies in converting resources into durable institutions capable of producing knowledge long after the donor’s personal reputation has faded.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ thread asking why billionaires do not fund long-term science projects.

clips.text_zh: Splits廢用，除非時間逼到冇得揀。全身練3至5次一星期完全冇問題：OHP、bench、DL、squat、pullup加accessories放同一節。肥仔信今日又叫我去gym，靠AI續命靠晒，至少重訓嘅重量係真實。
clips.text_en_b1: Splits are retarded unless they are necessary due to time constraints. There is literally nothing wrong with doing full-body training 3 to 5 times a week. There is nothing wrong with doing OHP, bench, deadlift, squat, pull-ups, and various accessories in the same session. My full session looks like this: pull-ups to failure, OHP 5x5, more pull-ups, deadlift 5x1, bench 5x5, squat 3x5.
clips.text_en_b2: Splits are pointless unless time constraints genuinely force them onto you, because there is absolutely nothing wrong with training the whole body three to five times a week. You can perform OHP, bench press, deadlifts, squats, pull-ups, and various accessories within the same session without any real problem. My own full-body session looks like this: pull-ups to failure, OHP 5x5, more pull-ups, deadlift 5x1, bench 5x5, and squat 3x5. As long as the weights keep going up, the results speak for themselves.
clips.text_en_c1: Splits are retarded unless time constraints leave you with no other option. There is literally nothing wrong with training full-body three to five times a week, and nothing wrong whatsoever with pressing OHP, bench, deadlift, squat, pull-ups, and assorted accessories inside the same session. My own full session runs roughly like this: pull-ups to failure, OHP 5x5, more pull-ups, deadlift 5x1, bench 5x5, and squat 3x5. A fat guy at the gym told me today that I should be doing splits, which is a rich recommendation from a man who keeps his progress alive with AI assistance. At least the weights I am putting up are real.
clips.text_en_c2: Body splits are largely unnecessary unless severe time constraints leave you with no alternative. There is nothing inherently wrong with training the entire body three to five times per week, nor with combining the overhead press, bench press, deadlift, squat, pull-ups, and supporting accessories in a single session. My own routine runs as follows: pull-ups to failure, overhead press five sets of five, additional pull-ups, deadlift five sets of one, bench press five sets of five, and squat three sets of five. The sequencing may look unconventional, but the principle is entirely sound: each session develops the body comprehensively rather than fragmenting it into narrow weekly priorities. Progress comes from consistent volume, appropriate loading, recovery, and gradual progression. The weights I record after each hard set are, at least, something real.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ thread defending frequent full-body workouts over split routines.

clips.text_zh: Eren嘅genocide plan成功，Zeke嘅euthanasia plan都成功。兩套計畫都「work」，但humanity死晒八成，Eldians又冇晒power of titan，全世界更加恨佢哋。係Isayama被逼寫咁差？定係AoT由頭到尾就爛，係我哋當年冇睇出？
clips.text_en_b1: Zeke's euthanasia plan works. Eren's genocide plan works. Both plans are great, yet we somehow end with 80% of humans wiped out. Eldians are now left without power of Titan shifting, and the whole world hates them 100 times more. Was Isayama threatened into making such a shitty ending, or was AoT bad from the start and we just didn't notice?
clips.text_en_b2: Zeke's euthanasia plan succeeds, and Eren's genocide plan succeeds as well, so somehow both ideas work out despite being completely opposed. The result, however, is that 80% of humanity is wiped out, the Eldians lose their power of Titan shifting entirely, and the rest of the world ends up hating them a hundred times more than before. So was Isayama forced into producing such an awful ending, or was Attack on Titan broken from the very beginning, and we were simply too invested to notice?
clips.text_en_c1: Zeke's euthanasia plan works, and Eren's genocide plan works as well. Both schemes are supposedly brilliant, and yet somehow eighty percent of humanity is wiped out in the process. The Eldians are left without the power of Titan shifting, and the rest of the world now hates them a hundred times more than before. Which raises the obvious question: was Isayama pressured into writing such an atrocious ending, or was Attack on Titan rotten from the very first chapter and none of us noticed at the time?
clips.text_en_c2: Zeke’s euthanasia plan succeeds, and Eren’s genocide plan succeeds; somehow, both schemes are presented as workable even though humanity is reduced by eighty percent and the Eldians lose the power of the Titans. The world emerges far more hostile toward them than before, which makes the conclusion difficult to reconcile with the story’s earlier themes. Was Hajime Isayama pressured into writing such an incoherent ending, or was Attack on Titan flawed from its inception, and did audiences simply fail to recognize the rot concealed beneath its dramatic momentum? Both possibilities are dispiriting. If the former, then the ending was an act of creative compromise; if the latter, every promising arc and character development was compromised long before the finale. The ending does not merely disappoint, but actively contradicts much of what preceded it.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ thread debating Attack on Titan's ending and its moral outcomes.

Over the past few weeks, the realisation has become impossible to ignore. There is no meaningful tokenisation, and no fresh capital is entering the market. Ethereum, which does very little, has been sold as a scientific project run by a bunch of assholes who merely smell their own farts. It will not be adopted. Fine: another tuition fee, another lesson learned.
clips.text_en_c2: I have finally reached enlightenment, however unwelcome the news may be: crypto is dead. For years I remained a 100 percent ETH bagholder, emotionally married to my bags, patiently waiting for one of those seductive narratives to propel ETH to $10,000. Over the past few weeks, the cold arithmetic became impossible to ignore: no tokenization, no fresh capital entering the ecosystem, and Ethereum itself accomplishing precious little beyond existing. The project resembles a science experiment run by a clique of、消费 self-congratulatory narcissists who mistake their own flatulence for progress. There will be no mainstream adoption. So be it; tuition paid, and an expensive lesson learned.

clips.text_zh: Serious thread。我有 50萬歐擺住冇用，考慮 all in NVDA。睇下事實：1) AI 唔會消失，你唔做AI，人地做然後 dominate，等於唔造核彈，你負擔唔起唔造。美國負擔得起。2) Jensen 要麼係白痴，要麼係間諜，我覺得當間諜太離譜。btw 啲 AI 股今日食晒爛，邊個仲有膽接刀？
clips.text_en_b1: Serious thread. I've got half a million euros doing nothing and I'm considering going all in on NVDA. Let's look at the facts: 1) AI is not going anywhere. If you are not developing AI, China is developing AI and will dominate. This is like not building the nuke. You cannot afford not to, so you will if you can. And the US can.
clips.text_en_b2: Serious thread. I have half a million euros sitting idle, and I am considering going all in on NVDA. Let us examine the facts: first, AI is not going away. If we refuse to develop it, China will, gain control, and dominate the field. It is like declining to build the bomb because you dislike what it represents. clips.text_en_c1: Serious thread. I have half a million euros sitting idle, and I am considering going all in on NVDA. Let us examine the facts. First, AI is not going away; if we refuse to develop it, China will, dominate the field, and leave us with no viable option. It is comparable to declining to build the bomb: you cannot afford not to pursue such technology if you have the capacity, and the US does. Second, Jensen Huang is either an idiot or a spy, and I think the spy explanation is absurd. By the way, AI-related stocks were hammered today, so who still has the balls to buy the dip?
clips.text_en_c2: A serious thread, because I have half a million euros doing nothing, and I am seriously considering going all in on NVDA. Examine the fundamentals rather than the chart. First, artificial intelligence is not going away; those who refuse to develop it merely cede the initiative to competitors who will dominate the field, much as a nation that declines to build a nuclear arsenal cannot then complain that its adversaries have done so. You cannot afford not to pursue it, and the United States can certainly afford it. Second, Jensen Huang is either an idiot or a spy, and I suspect the spy hypothesis is absurd. By the way, the AI stocks were savaged today, so who still has the stomach to catch the falling knife?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ OP with 500k EUR idle, weighing an all-in NVDA position.

clips.source_hint: /g/ thread linking CNBC and NYT coverage of a second Jensen Huang affair.

clips.text_en_c2: Where has all the hype surrounding Elon's flying car gone? clips.text_en_c2: Tesla plunged 11%, with no apparent catalyst to explain the rout. Rather than reacting to any meaningful deterioration in the company’s underlying business, investors appear to have treated the move as a familiar meme-stock sell-off. That interpretation makes grimly logical sense: if the entire enterprise is regarded as a joke, even an inexplicable decline requires no elaborate explanation. The share price fell because it fell, which is precisely what one might expect when fundamentals have been overshadowed by the belief that the company itself is, in the market’s collective judgement, something of a joke.

clips.text_en_c1: Why is Tesla competing with Toyota so aggressively? Toyota earned six times more profit than Tesla last year, yet Tesla’s market capitalisation remains higher than that of the next 37 automakers combined. On earnings alone, the valuation looks irrational; if the figures are being compared on a consistent basis, it is difficult to defend. The poster’s point is not necessarily that Tesla cannot succeed, but that investors appear willing to overlook its comparatively modest profitability in pursuit of growth, narrative, and technological prestige.
clips.text_en_c2: Why is Tesla competing with Toyota so fiercely when the financial fundamentals appear so lopsided? Toyota earned six times Tesla’s profit last year, yet Tesla’s market value remains higher than that of the next 37 automakers combined. Taken at face value, the comparison makes the valuation assigned to Tesla look wildly irrational. Unless, of course, investors are pricing in something other than present-day earnings—perhaps autonomy, energy storage, software, or Tesla’s perceived technological identity—and regard Toyota as a comparatively conventional manufacturer. The poster, however, sees the disparity simply as the market embracing a valuation that cannot plausibly be reconciled with established automotive economics.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ thread compares Tesla’s valuation with Toyota’s profit.

clips.text_en_b1: 1/2/3/4/5 is the ultimate test of whether someone is strong: one-plate overhead press for four reps, two-plate bench press for three reps, three-plate squat for two reps, four-plate deadlift for one rep, and five strict pull-ups.

clips.text_en_c1: The 1/2/3/4/5 challenge is presented as the ultimate test of whether somebody is genuinely strong. Complete a one-plate overhead press for four repetitions, a two-plate bench press for three, a three-plate squat for two, a four-plate deadlift for one, and five strict pull-ups. It is a demanding sequence because each exercise demands both technical control and substantial absolute strength. Although the standards sound straightforward, the combined challenge is severe: failing at any stage could expose weaknesses that a conventional lift would otherwise conceal.
clips.text_en_c2: The 1/2/3/4/5 protocol is billed as the ultimate strength test, although it demands considerably more than conventional gym proficiency. The lifter must complete four repetitions of an overhead press with one plate, three reps of the bench press with two plates, two reps of a squat with three plates, a single deadlift rep with four plates, and five strict pull-ups. Each successive station combines increasing load with decreasing repetitions, culminating in an especially demanding sequence of explosive and technical movements. Success therefore requires not merely raw force, but the mobility, coordination, balance, and sheer grit needed to preserve strict form under increasingly punishing circumstances.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ post proposes a five-part strength test with exact lifts and reps.

clips.text_en_c1: Tesla has fallen by 11% for what the poster describes as no fucking reason, with the dramatic decline visible across the TSLA chart and prompting an emphatic claim that the entire company is merely a meme. The language conveys anger and disbelief rather than a measured financial diagnosis, and it offers no fundamental catalyst for the sell-off. There is also no specific trading level, entry point, or exit target proposed. Instead, the post captures the emotional impact of a sharp overnight or intraday move, illustrating how quickly confidence in a high-profile stock can collapse when the price chart delivers a painful reversal without an obvious explanation.
clips.text_en_c2: Tesla has crashed by 11% for no fucking reason, and the poster dismisses the entire company as a meme. clips.text_zh: Coding by hand. Drawing by hand. Writing your own texts. Modelling by hand. Composing songs. Doing your own research. AI 將會令大部分人乜都唔做，靠AI續命就真係冇救了。
clips.text_en_b1: The post says hand coding, drawing, writing, modelling, composing songs, research, and reading long articles may all become obsolete because of AI. It warns of a two-tier society where most people delegate everything and let their brains turn to mush.
clips.text_en_b2: The post imagines a future in which hand-coding, drawing, writing your own texts, modelling, composing songs, conducting your own research, and even reading lengthy articles all become obsolete because of AI. What worries the writer most is that most people will simply delegate everything to machines. Although the technology may still be useful, relying on it entirely leaves little room for personal effort. The warning is blunt: if your brain turns to mush, you are probably beyond saving.
clips.text_en_c1: The post imagines a future in which several conventional skills become obsolete: hand coding, drawing, writing original texts, modelling by hand, composing songs, conducting independent research, and reading lengthy articles. Rather than celebrating that prospect, the author appears deeply sceptical, warning that most people may eventually delegate virtually every task to AI and rely on it simply to sustain their lives. Such dependence could produce a stark two-tier society, divided between those who retain the capacity to think and create independently and those whose brains, as the poster puts it, turn to mush.
clips.text_en_c2: The post imagines AI making a range of human skills obsolete: coding by hand, drawing by hand, writing original texts, modelling, composing songs, conducting research, and reading long articles. Its central warning is not merely that machines will perform these tasks more efficiently, but that most people will surrender responsibility for them and become passive consumers of automated output. If everyone delegates the difficult work, the brain loses the exercise it needs to remain sharp, and a two-tier society may emerge, divided between those capable of directing technology and those whose minds have turned to mush. The catalogue of activities is therefore less a prediction than a lament: reliance on AI to sustain one’s existence may leave little worth preserving.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread warning that AI may make people abandon practical and creative skills.

clips.text_zh: The Cybertruck is dead. On November 6, Reuters reported that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027. Musk called it the end of an era.
clips.text_en_b1: Reuters reported on November 6 that Tesla will end Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027. Musk called the wind-down the end of an era, after years of persistently weak sales.
clips.text_en_b2: Reuters reported on November 6 that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027. Musk described the decision as the end of an era, although the announcement itself carried little surprise given years of persistently weak sales. The Cybertruck, once presented as a bold new direction for the company, has struggled to gain traction with buyers. Even so, the wind-down reportedly concerns production rather than an immediate end to the vehicle itself.
clips.text_en_c1: According to Reuters, which reported the development on November 6, Tesla is expected to wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027. Musk characterised the decision as the end of an era, a phrase that neatly captures the model's uneasy trajectory since its highly public launch. Although the announcement is presented as the beginning of a production wind-down, the Cybertruck had already struggled commercially for years, with persistently weak sales failing to generate the sustained demand many observers had anticipated.
clips.text_en_c2: Reuters reported on November 6 that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027. Musk described the decision as the end of an era, a suitably dramatic phrase for a model whose long-running commercial difficulties have gradually eroded its prospects. After years of persistently weak sales, the announcement turns the Cybertruck from an ambitious electric pickup into a fading chapter in Tesla’s product history. The report does not, however, offer a detailed account of the production schedule, the scale of the retrenchment, or the effect on employment at the Texas facility. It instead foregrounds the timing and Musk’s own framing, presenting the wind-down as both a logistical decision and a symbolic conclusion.
clips.source_hint: A news post about Tesla ending Cybertruck production at its Texas factory.

clips.text_zh: Whitepill Thread. Hot cocoa is the best pre-workout, anyone can start lifting, and you can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months. Less than a year, people will notice you lift. Just eat some protein and avoid fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_b1: This whitepill thread says anyone can start lifting without sports experience. It claims that people can escape skinnyfat mode in under six months and show visible progress within one year. It also recommends protein, avoiding fast food, candy, and soda, and says a gym membership is unnecessary.
clips.text_en_b2: This whitepill thread argues that absolutely anyone can start lifting weights, even without any sporting experience, and that hot cocoa is the ultimate pre-workout drink. It claims people can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months, with visible progress showing up within a year, because other people will notice that you lift. The advice is refreshingly simple: eat plenty of protein, avoid fast food, candy, and soda, and forget about joining a gym, since a membership is completely unnecessary.
clips.text_en_c1: This upbeat whitepill thread argues that anyone can begin lifting weights, regardless of previous sporting experience, and that no gym membership is necessary. It presents hot cocoa as the ideal pre-workout drink while encouraging beginners to take the first step without overcomplicating matters. According to the post, someone stuck in skinnyfat mode can escape that phase in less than six months, with people noticing visible lifting progress within a year. The basic advice is to eat sufficient protein and avoid fast food, candy, and soda. Although the claims are optimistic and oversimplified, the message is straightforward: consistent training and sensible dietary habits can produce noticeable changes, even for complete newcomers.
clips.text_en_c2: This whitepill thread presents weightlifting as an accessible route to physical improvement for anyone, regardless of sporting experience. Its central claim is that a newcomer can escape “skinnyfat mode” in less than six months and produce visible lifting progress within a year, provided the fundamentals are respected. Hot cocoa is nominated as the ideal pre-workout, although the thread’s practical advice ultimately rests on uncomplicated discipline: eat sufficient protein, avoid fast food, candy, and soda, and begin training. A gym membership is considered unnecessary, since the message emphasizes consistency rather than equipment or commercial facilities. The post is deliberately reassuring, replacing intimidating expertise with the promise that ordinary people can make measurable progress if they simply start.
clips.source_hint: A beginner-friendly fitness thread about lifting, diet, and visible progress.

clips.text_zh: They censored all mentions of the Deku Tree dying. It is rated E10, so ten-year-olds can handle it. They kept Death Mountain and the graveyard anyway, so what is the point of censoring death?
clips.text_en_b1: The poster says the game censored mentions of the Deku Tree dying, even though it is rated E10. They argue that ten-year-olds can handle the subject. Since Death Mountain and the graveyard remained, the censorship makes little sense.
clips.text_en_b2: The poster claims that the game censored every mention of the Deku Tree dying, which seems absurd given that it carries an E10 rating specifically meant for children aged ten and above. In other words, if ten-year-olds can handle the subject, the censorship makes very little sense. Although the developers apparently drew a line somewhere, they kept Death Mountain and the graveyard in the game. The writer cannot understand why death itself was protected while these elements remained untouched.
clips.text_en_c1: The poster claims that every mention of the Deku Tree dying has been censored, despite the game carrying an E10 rating intended for audiences aged ten and older. If ten-year-olds are considered old enough for the material in question, the author asks, why are they supposedly not ready for this particular reference? The criticism gains force from the fact that Death Mountain and the graveyard remain available in the game. Since these more explicit death-related elements have not been removed, selectively censoring the Deku Tree appears inconsistent.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster claims that the game censored every mention of the Deku Tree’s death, despite carrying an E10 rating intended for audiences aged ten and above. Their argument is straightforward: if children that young can negotiate the game’s existing themes, there is no coherent reason to conceal this particular instance of mortality. The inconsistency becomes still more glaring because Death Mountain and the graveyard were retained rather than removed. In other words, the supposedly protective edit leaves far more explicit symbols of death readily accessible while banning discussion of a tree’s demise. The complaint is therefore not about violence in the abstract, but about editorial arbitrariness. If the setting already embraces graveyards and ominous mountains, censoring the Deku Tree appears less a meaningful safeguard than a strangely selective gesture.
clips.source_hint: A /v/ thread criticizing censorship of the Deku Tree’s death in a game remake.

clips.text_zh: 我係SEA嘅brownoid。20萬美元喺第一世界標準睇落冇乜，但喺我哋呢度夠四代人食。Bitcoin、time deposit，定gold bars邊個最安全？真係唔知，lol。
clips.text_en_b1: I’m a brownoid from SEA, and $200,000 is nothing by first-world standards. Here, it could feed my family for four generations. People are telling me to buy Bitcoin, use a time deposit, or buy gold bars. I don’t know which option is safest.

clips.text_en_b1: Tesla crashed 11% for no fucking reason. The entire company is a meme. Sometimes the stock just decides to become a meme again, and the charts show why fundamentals cannot control everything.

Sometimes the stock just decides to become a meme again, although no amount of analysis can explain why. clips.text_en_c1: Tesla crashed 11% for no fucking reason, because the entire company is basically a meme. Sometimes the stock simply decides to become a meme again, and the charts demonstrate why fundamentals cannot control everything. Even if the business appears sound on paper, market sentiment can overwhelm logic in an instant. clips.text_en_c2: Tesla crashed by 11% for absolutely no fucking reason, because the entire company is basically a meme. A company can coast on artificial intelligence for a while, but sooner or later the numbers put the lie on trial.

clips.text_zh: 年輕人應該有cheap、abundant housing嘅選擇。Mass-scale生產小型manufactured houses同studio apartments，結構仍然sound，價錢就得盡量平。點解 regulations 唔肯咁做？原來係要keep inflating boomer property values，靠，咁撈法真係fucked up。
clips.text_en_b1: People should have the option of cheap, abundant housing, especially for young people. Small manufactured houses and studio apartments could be mass-produced and made structurally sound. But regulations prevent this and keep inflating boomer property values. It’s really fucked up.
clips.text_en_b2: People, especially young people, should have access to cheap and abundant housing. Small manufactured houses and studio apartments could be mass-produced while remaining structurally sound, so why won’t regulations allow that? Instead, the system keeps propping up boomer property values and restricting the supply of affordable homes. This arrangement is completely fucked up, because it transfers enormous wealth to older property owners while leaving younger people behind.
clips.text_en_c1: People, especially young people, should have access to cheap and abundant housing. Small manufactured houses and studio apartments could be mass-produced, provided they remain structurally sound and are sold for the lowest practicable price. Yet regulations prevent that kind of development and, in doing so, keep inflating older people’s property values. If the planning system were genuinely intended to increase housing supply, it would permit these simple, high-density alternatives instead of protecting scarcity. That arrangement is thoroughly fucked up, particularly for anyone who cannot afford the inflated market.
clips.text_en_c2: People, particularly young people, should have access to cheap and abundant housing rather than being priced out of the market altogether. Small manufactured houses and studio apartments could be mass-produced, provided they remain structurally sound and are sold for as little as possible. Why can’t regulations permit that? The obstacle is a deeply entrenched system that keeps inflating older generations’ property values and treats scarcity as preferable to construction. The result is grotesque: abundant land and abundant labour are converted into unaffordable boxes while established owners rake in the gains. It is comprehensively fucked up.
clips.source_hint: The OP argues for cheaper mass-produced housing and criticizes regulations.
