clips.text_en_c1: What is your solid plan if large language models eventually replace you? Farming, trades, or something else entirely? The question appeared in the tech section tonight, and there are no definitive answers. Engineering and site work may also be reshaped by AI, since routine technical tasks and skilled labour can both be automated or delegated to machines. If your current profession depends on knowledge that can be generated at scale, waiting until displacement is imminent would be a mistake. A practical backup, developed while you still have time and income, would be considerably wiser.
clips.text_en_c2: Suppose large language models really do replace you at work. What, exactly, is your solid plan? Farming? Skilled trades? The question appeared in the tech section tonight, and there were no clear answers, because even supposedly secure paths are exposed. Engineering may be automated, site work may be reshaped by robotics, and professional certification can no longer guarantee that a trade will remain untouched. Of course, one could defer the problem and work it out when the disruption actually arrives, but that would be rather convenient. A practical backup, cultivated while one still has time and income, would be considerably wiser.
clips.source_hint: A tech thread asks what people will do after LLM replacement.

clips.text_zh: 點解要理股票market crash？AI-related business根本冇direct profit from AI，AI只係hype machine。SpaceX更加用Starlink legitimate profit養自己，再包裝成AI business，估值先可以到trillion dollars。股票本來係means for an end，AI business個end反而係stock valuation，market cap同AI冇半個銀仔關係，膠膠吶。
clips.text_en_b1: Why care about the stock market crash? AI-related businesses lack direct profit from AI. AI is just a hype machine. SpaceX uses legitimate Starlink profit to present itself as an AI company worth a trillion dollars. For AI businesses, the stock valuation becomes the actual end.
clips.text_en_b2: Why should anyone care about a stock market crash when many AI-related businesses generate no direct profit from AI? AI has become little more than a hype machine. SpaceX, for example, uses legitimate profits from Starlink to present itself as an AI business and justify a trillion-dollar valuation. This turns the usual relationship inside out: the stock valuation becomes the end, whereas the market cap has virtually nothing to do with AI itself. Pretty ridiculous, honestly.
clips.text_en_c1: Why should anyone care about a stock-market crash when AI-related businesses generate no direct profit from AI? AI is merely a hype machine. SpaceX, for example, uses legitimate profits from Starlink to present itself as an AI company capable of reaching a trillion-dollar valuation. Stocks are supposed to be a means to an end, but for many supposed AI businesses, the end is the stock valuation itself. If market capitalisation has no meaningful connection to AI revenue or performance, then investors are effectively paying for a narrative rather than a functioning enterprise.
clips.text_en_c2: Why should anyone care about a stock-market crash when many AI-related businesses generate no direct profit from AI itself? AI has become little more than a hype machine, capable of attaching an extraordinary valuation to companies whose economics have little obvious connection to the technology. SpaceX offers the clearest example: legitimate Starlink profits support the business, while the enterprise is repackaged as an AI company so its valuation can reach a trillion dollars. Stocks are ordinarily merely a means of financing an enterprise, but for many AI businesses the share price has become the destination itself. Market capitalisation and artificial intelligence are connected by approximately half a cent.
clips.source_hint: The OP claims AI companies rely more on market valuation than direct AI profits.

clips.text_en_b1: Impact of the midterm results tomorrow on financial markets. Any bets? I think that if the results are red, we pump like crazy. If they are blue, we take a fucked-up dive. The market will move sharply either way, so this is the important macro bet right now.
clips.text_en_b2: How will financial markets react when tomorrow’s midterm results come in? I’m placing my bets: if the red states win, the market could pump like crazy, whereas a blue victory might send it into a deep dive. Because Hong Kong’s trading range is so narrow, any breakout will be difficult to stop or cut losses quickly, especially if several CFD positions get blown. clips.text_en_c1: The case for investing exclusively in compute is that it represents the scarce input on which so many other businesses depend. Neoclouds, by contrast, are largely resellers of capacity, while software carries the distinct risk that AI will absorb much of its functionality. The underlying argument is simple: owning the infrastructure that powers AI may offer a more defensible position than betting on its many downstream applications.

clips.text_en_c1: The barbell hack squat happens to suit this lifter particularly well because it places less strain on the lower back than either the squat or the deadlift. Another advantage is that the lifter is unlikely to become pinned beneath the bar: if a repetition fails, dropping it is comparatively straightforward. Hamstring contact also provides a useful built-in check on form, since improper movement causes the bar to strike the legs. Given these benefits, the obvious question is why the exercise is not used more widely.
clips.text_en_c2: The barbell hack squat is exceptionally well suited to me, particularly because it places less strain on the lower back than either the squat or the deadlift. Although this remains an opinion, the post clearly favors gold over Bitcoin at the moment.
clips.text_en_c1: Have you followed the latest developments in artificial intelligence and the threat they pose to Bitcoin? If I were you, I would buy gold now. Set Bitcoin and gold side by side, and the momentum behind AI is becoming increasingly alarming. As AI continues to improve, Bitcoin may face a considerably bigger challenge ahead, whereas gold appears to be the safer option. The post clearly favours gold over Bitcoin at this particular moment, although that does not make the recommendation a guarantee of future performance.
clips.text_en_c2: Have you been following recent advances in artificial intelligence and the mounting threat they pose to Bitcoin? If I were you, I would buy gold now, because placing Bitcoin and gold side by side makes the AI narrative increasingly difficult to ignore. As the technology continues to strengthen, Bitcoin may be facing a considerably more serious challenge ahead of it. Although the precise impact remains uncertain, the prevailing mood is unmistakably bullish toward gold. The post therefore signals a clear preference for traditional precious metals over Bitcoin at present, however speculative such a comparison may ultimately prove.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post says AI threatens Bitcoin and recommends buying gold.

clips.text_zh: Compute 先係你唯一應該投資嘅嘢。股票又好，真實晶片又好。Semi、Nvidia 都得。Neocloud 只係轉售商，自己冇 product 同 software。AI 可能食晒 software，連 hyperscaler 都未必安全。Google 試過 implement AI，反而 killing 自己 search ad business。科技太猛，優化 business 途中可能直接 wipe it out。靠，今個年代仲要靠AI續命。
clips.text_en_b1: Compute is the only thing you should invest in, whether that means stocks or physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are the main ideas. Neoclouds are only resellers without their own products, while software is risky because AI may eat it. Even hyperscalers face trouble: Google is damaging its search ad business while implementing AI.
clips.text_en_b2: Compute is the only thing you should invest in, whether that means buying shares or physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are the main ideas, whereas neoclouds are merely resellers with neither their own products nor their own software. Software is risky because AI may swallow whole categories of businesses. Even hyperscalers are not safe, as Google is damaging its search advertising business while implementing AI. Technology is advancing so quickly that optimisation can wipe out the original business.
clips.text_en_c1: Compute is the only asset I would seriously consider investing in, whether that means buying shares in semiconductor companies or acquiring physical chips. The main ideas are semis and Nvidia. Neoclouds, by contrast, are merely resellers with neither their own products nor their own software, which makes them considerably less compelling. Software is also risky because AI may gradually absorb many of its functions. Even hyperscalers are not immune: Google, for example, appears to be damaging its search advertising business while implementing AI. In such a rapidly evolving industry, optimisation can end up wiping out the very business it is meant to strengthen.
clips.text_en_c2: Compute is the one asset class you should seriously consider investing in, whether through equities or ownership of physical chips. Semiconductors and Nvidia are the principal ideas, whereas neoclouds appear to function merely as resellers, with neither proprietary products nor distinctive software of their own. Software itself is precarious, since AI may absorb much of the value it currently creates. Even hyperscalers are not immune: Google has been implementing AI while undermining its own search-advertising business. In technology, optimisation can be so disruptive that it wipes out the very business it is intended to strengthen.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post argues that compute, chips, and semiconductors are the strongest investment theme.

clips.text_zh: 有人話 load path 只係背書，講完就算。但我哋做 structural work，最怕 load path 講唔清。Beam 接到 column，column 落到 foundation，force 點樣傳，點解嗰個 member 咁做，全部都要 check。靠AI續命都要自己識睇图，唔可以只靠 AI 砌故事。
clips.text_en_b1: Understand how loads travel through a structure. Loads move through beams, columns, connections, and foundations. A civil engineer must explain why each member exists and how it was checked. This basic knowledge helps when reviewing drawings and discussing work with contractors on site.
clips.text_en_b2: Some people treat load paths as nothing more than jargon to memorise before moving on. However, structural work becomes dangerous when nobody can explain how forces actually travel. You need to know how a beam connects to a column, how the column transfers its load into the foundation, and why each member has been designed in that particular way. AI may keep us employed, but engineers still need to read drawings and build sound judgements rather than simply asking it to invent convincing stories.
clips.text_en_c1: Some people treat load paths as little more than paperwork: identify the system, draw an arrow, and move on. Yet anyone doing structural work knows that failing to explain how forces travel can be dangerous. Loads pass from beams into columns, through connections, and ultimately into foundations, so every member must be justified. When reviewing drawings or discussing structural decisions with contractors on site, it is essential to understand why each component exists and how it has been checked. AI may help engineers keep pace, but it cannot replace the judgement required to read drawings rather than merely generate plausible-sounding stories.
clips.text_en_c2: Some dismiss load-path analysis as little more than rote theory: explain the principle, tick the box, and move on. Yet anyone engaged in structural work knows that an incomprehensible load path is a source of profound anxiety. How does a beam transfer force into a column? How does that column carry the load into the foundation? Why is each member proportioned and arranged as it is? Every aspect must be checked. AI may keep us employed, but it cannot substitute for the ability to read drawings critically and interrogate the underlying engineering story.
clips.source_hint: The gaming thread describes growing overwhelmed as quests become more complicated.

clips.text_zh: Future is coming at you, anons。Claude 依家已經開始做 brain surgery，仲係其中一個 hardest fields。靠AI續命真係唔係講笑。AI 可能先食 blue collar，再食 white collar。Professional exam 都未考完，唔可以淨係靠 AI 幫我讀書。
clips.text_en_b1: The future is coming at us, anons. Claude is now doing brain surgery, one of the hardest fields for anyone to master. This development shows how quickly AI is moving into serious professional work. However, AI cannot replace the knowledge needed for engineering exams and site decisions.
clips.text_en_b2: The future is coming at us, anons, and Claude has already begun performing brain surgery, which is among the hardest fields anyone can master. Clearly, this is no longer some distant prospect, so relying on AI to keep us employed is hardly a joke. AI may first replace blue-collar work and then move into white-collar professions. Even so, it cannot supply the underlying knowledge required to pass professional engineering exams or make sound decisions on site.
clips.text_en_c1: The future is coming at us, anons, and Claude is already being used in brain surgery, one of the most demanding fields anyone can master. That development demonstrates how quickly AI is moving into serious professional work, rather than merely handling routine office tasks. AI may first displace blue-collar roles and then move into white-collar professions, although this does not mean expertise has become irrelevant. If you have not even finished your professional examinations, you cannot rely on AI to complete your education for you. It may assist with learning, but the underlying knowledge required for engineering exams and on-site decisions still has to be yours.
clips.text_en_c2: The future is bearing down on us, anons. Claude is already being used in brain surgery, one of the most exacting and difficult fields any professional must master. This is not a trivial application or a convenient thought experiment; it illustrates how rapidly AI is advancing into work where mistakes may have irreversible consequences. The broader implication is equally unsettling: AI may first displace blue-collar work and subsequently erode many white-collar professions. Nevertheless, no system can replace the foundational knowledge required to pass professional examinations, exercise sound judgement on site, and recognise when an automated recommendation should not be trusted.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ post says Claude is now performing brain surgery.

clips.text_zh: Tesla police car？我覺得 Elon 可能搞緊自己嘅 private police force。之後 local government 為咗 save money，甚至叫 Elon 負責 police officers 嘅 salary，變成佢自己嘅 private army。香港咁逼嘅地方，會唔會遲一日都咁玩？
clips.text_en_b1: A Tesla police car has appeared, and I think Elon may be setting up his own private police force. Local governments could later pay Elon to cover police officers' salaries to save money. That would turn the officers into his private army. This is an extreme speculation about public spending and policing.
clips.text_en_b2: A Tesla police car has appeared, and I suspect Elon may be setting up his own private police force. Local governments could eventually pay him to cover the salaries of police officers, because that would save them money. If that happened, the officers would effectively become his private army. This is an extreme and highly speculative scenario, but given how desperate public finances have become, could Hong Kong end up following the same route one day?
clips.text_en_c1: A Tesla police car has apparently appeared, which makes me wonder whether Elon Musk is quietly developing a private police force. If local governments later pay him to cover the salaries of police officers in order to reduce public spending, those officers could effectively become his private army. The logic is simple: use public money to finance personnel who ultimately serve a private enterprise. This remains an extreme speculation rather than an established arrangement, but it raises uncomfortable questions about accountability, public expenditure, and the future of policing. Given how constrained Hong Kong is, could the same model eventually be adopted here?
clips.text_en_c2: A Tesla police car has appeared, and I suspect Elon may be assembling his own private police force. If local governments later pay him to cover the salaries of police officers in order to reduce public expenditure, those officers could effectively become his private army. This is, admittedly, an extreme conjecture about policing, public spending, and corporate power, but the underlying direction of travel is not impossible to imagine. Given how financially compressed Hong Kong is, could a place under such pressure eventually adopt a comparable arrangement? The proposal remains speculative, yet its practical implications are worth taking seriously.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ thread jokes that Elon is creating a private police force.

clips.text_zh: 有人話 squat 根本唔係 lifting，亦唔 mimic 日常需要做嘅動作，仲有 injury risk。應該做 deadlift、bench、OHP 同 cardio。肥仔信今日又叫我去 gym，但我最怕 leg day。Squat 係咪真係咁冇用？
clips.text_en_b1: Some people say squats are not even lifting because they do not copy normal daily movements. They also claim that squats have a high injury risk and provide little benefit. They recommend deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardio instead. What is your view on squat training?
clips.text_en_b2: Some people argue that squats are not even a real lifting movement because they fail to imitate actions required in everyday life. They also claim that squats carry a high injury risk while providing little benefit, recommending deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardio instead. A fat friend asked me to visit the gym again today, although leg day is the one I dread most. So, are squats genuinely that useless?
clips.text_en_c1: Some critics maintain that squats are not true lifting because they do not replicate ordinary movements of daily life. They also argue that the exercise carries a substantial injury risk while providing comparatively little benefit. Their preferred alternatives are deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardio, which supposedly offer a more balanced training programme. A fat man told me today that I should go to the gym again, although leg day remains my greatest nightmare. So, are squats genuinely that useless, or are their critics confusing a complicated exercise with one that lacks functional value?
clips.text_en_c2: Some argue that squats are not genuine lifting because they fail to replicate ordinary movements of daily life. They also contend that the exercise carries a substantial injury risk while offering comparatively little benefit, recommending deadlifts, bench presses, overhead presses, curls, and cardiovascular work instead. Fat Cat told me to go to the gym again today, but leg day remains the part of training I dread most. Is the case against squats really as conclusive as its supporters suggest? Their argument sounds superficially persuasive, although it appears to confuse general usefulness with the peculiar demands of competitive strength training.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ thread argues that deadlifts and other lifts are better than squats.

clips.text_zh: Black Clover 做咗 October 2026 Crunchyroll 最受歡迎 anime第一名，打贏 Dragon Ball Super: Beerus 同 The Apothecary Diaries Season 3。得返三個 BChads 喺 /a/ 跣住，確實係好消息。靠，追番終於有啲回報。
clips.text_en_b1: Black Clover is the most watched anime on Crunchyroll for October 2026. It has beaten Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Many fans may not care, but this is great news for the remaining Black Clover fans on /a/. The anime finally got some recognition.
clips.text_en_b2: Black Clover has reached number one among the most-watched anime on Crunchyroll for October 2026, beating Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Although plenty of casual fans may not care, this is undoubtedly excellent news for the remaining Black Clover fans on /a/. clips.text_en_c1: Black Clover has topped Crunchyroll’s most-watched anime rankings for October 2026, beating both Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Although many people may not care about the chart, it is unquestionably good news for the remaining Black Clover fans on /a/. After following the series for so long, they have finally received a measure of recognition for their patience and loyalty. More importantly, the result suggests that Black Clover has achieved genuine mainstream visibility rather than remaining confined to its established audience, which is a notable achievement for any long-running series.
clips.text_en_c2: Black Clover has secured the number-one position among the most-watched anime on Crunchyroll for October 2026, overtaking both Dragon Ball Super: Beerus and The Apothecary Diaries Season 3. Plenty of casual viewers may remain indifferent to the ranking, but it is undeniably welcome news for the remaining Black Clover enthusiasts on /a/. After such a long and sometimes frustrating wait, the series has finally received a measure of recognition that its most committed fans have long believed it deserved. Whatever reservations outsiders may retain about the anime, this achievement marks a genuinely significant moment for its audience.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ post reports Black Clover leading Crunchyroll's October 2026 rankings.

clips.text_zh: 法國真係玩完。119% debt to GDP，5.4% deficit，國會又開唔到budget。OAT-Bund spread 開始爆。鬧鬼同散戶淨係望住Bitcoin，歐洲個bag就 quietly dump 咗。靠AI續命，連睇法國財報都睇到一半。
clips.text_en_b1: France is basically cooked. Its debt is 119% of GDP, the deficit is 5.4%, and its parliament cannot pass a budget. The OAT-Bund spread is blowing out as the risk premium grows. Elites quietly dump European bags and flee to the dollar while retail stays distracted.
clips.text_en_b2: France is, quite simply, in serious trouble. Its debt stands at 119% of GDP, the budget deficit is 5.4%, and parliament still cannot get a budget passed. As the risk premium rises, the OAT-Bund spread is starting to blow out. Meanwhile, wealthy investors are quietly dumping European positions and fleeing to the dollar, whereas ordinary retail investors remain distracted by Bitcoin. Even AI cannot rescue the situation; people can barely stomach the latest French financial report.
clips.text_en_c1: France is, in a word, cooked. Public debt stands at 119% of GDP, the budget deficit is 5.4%, and parliament remains unable to pass a budget. As investors demand a higher risk premium, the OAT-Bund spread is beginning to blow out. While the political and financial elite quietly dump European assets and shift into dollars, ordinary retail investors remain distracted by Bitcoin. The whole story feels increasingly like an AI-powered attempt to keep the narrative alive, even when reading France’s financial results has become an exercise in futility.
clips.text_en_c2: France is, to put it bluntly, running out of road. Public debt stands at 119% of GDP, the budget deficit is 5.4%, and parliament remains incapable of passing a budget. As the risk premium climbs, the OAT-Bund spread is widening in earnest. Meanwhile, those at the top are quietly disposing of European assets and seeking refuge in dollars, whereas ordinary investors remain engrossed in Bitcoin. The attempt to prop up the narrative with artificial intelligence is not especially convincing; even watching France’s financial results becomes rather half-hearted when the underlying picture is this grim.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ warning about France’s debt, deficits, and the widening OAT-Bund spread.

clips.text_zh: XRP才是正主。Ripple 昨日正式拿到national bank charter，Scott Bessent 又做Swell headline speaker。Singapore仲有BLOOM initiative，同Malaysia、Thailand嘅央行一齊。靠AI續命：但追高入去CFD，唔係叫strategy，係叫送錢。
clips.text_en_b1: XRP is the standard. Ripple received final approval for a national bank charter yesterday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined its Swell event as the featured headline speaker. Ripple is also involved in Singapore’s BLOOM initiative with the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand.
clips.text_en_b2: XRP is the real headline here. Ripple finally received approval for a national bank charter yesterday, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appeared as the headline speaker at its Swell event. Ripple is also involved in Singapore’s BLOOM initiative, working alongside the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand. All of this makes XRP the centre of attention. However, chasing the token through CFDs is not a sound strategy; it is a quick way to hand your money away.
clips.text_en_c1: XRP is the real headline here. Ripple received final approval for a national bank charter yesterday, a significant regulatory milestone rather than another round of market speculation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent then joined Ripple’s Swell event as its featured headline speaker, reinforcing the company’s increasingly prominent institutional connections. Ripple is also participating in Singapore’s BLOOM initiative alongside the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand. That said, buying XRP on the assumption that it must rise, particularly through leveraged CFDs, is hardly a strategy; it is an expensive way of donating money to the market.
clips.text_en_c2: XRP, rather than the usual market favourites, deserves to be centre stage. Ripple received final approval for a national bank charter yesterday, a potentially consequential development for its regulatory standing. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent then appeared at Ripple’s Swell event as its headline speaker, providing the company with an unmistakably prestigious endorsement. Ripple is also participating in Singapore’s BLOOM initiative alongside the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand. One caveat remains: chasing the asset through leveraged CFDs is not strategy; it is an expensive way of donating money to the market.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post claiming Ripple received a national bank charter and listing recent regulatory developments.

clips.text_zh: 成班人淨係講AI，AI this，AI that。根本冇人理computing嘅freedom同privacy。美國同EU都有KIDS Act，其他國家亦都一齊出類似規例。目的就係令人冇辦法用任何running an operating system嘅電腦。靠AI續命，連私隱都靠唔住。
clips.text_en_b1: Everyone talks about AI and ignores freedom and privacy in computing. The US KIDS Act and the EU KIDS Act aim to make using any computer with an operating system difficult. Similar regulations are appearing in many countries at the same time, so surely that is a coincidence.
clips.text_en_b2: Everyone is talking about AI, AI this, AI that, while hardly anyone discusses the freedom and privacy that should underpin computing. Both the US KIDS Act and the EU KIDS Act are intended to make it difficult to use any computer that runs an operating system. Similar legislation is also appearing across numerous countries at the same time, so the coordinated direction is hard to dismiss as coincidence. The result is that even basic digital privacy is becoming increasingly difficult to maintain.
clips.text_en_c1: Everyone is preoccupied with AI, while the far more consequential questions surrounding computing freedom and personal privacy are quietly sidelined. The US KIDS Act and the EU KIDS Act are intended to make it difficult for ordinary users to operate any computer running an operating system, and comparable legislation is appearing across many countries simultaneously. If these measures genuinely have unrelated aims, the timing must be a remarkable coincidence. The broader concern is obvious: once basic autonomy is constrained, even the limited protections people believe privacy provides may prove difficult to maintain.
clips.text_en_c2: The public debate fixates on artificial intelligence while the far more fundamental questions of computing freedom and privacy are allowed to lapse. Both the American KIDS Act and its European counterpart seek to make ordinary computer use difficult wherever an operating system is involved. Similar restrictions are emerging across numerous countries at roughly the same moment, which is difficult to interpret as anything resembling coincidence. The effect, if these measures proceed, would be to place routine digital life under increasingly intrusive supervision. Whatever comfort artificial intelligence may provide, it plainly cannot compensate for the erosion of private autonomy.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ thread criticizing KIDS Act-style regulations and their impact on computing freedom and privacy.

clips.text_zh: 邊個話Dems想trans你個細路？Elon Musk？香港新聞就係咁，乜都變成政治鬥爭。AP都照開工，Tom cat同Sum Ho都唔會因為條thread停手。醒腦靠AI，錢靠prop firm，唔靠佢發言。
clips.text_en_b1: Who told you that Democrats want to transition your kids? Elon Musk? The post turns culture-war politics into a joke. It is another example of online arguments replacing actual discussion. The claim itself sounds completely absurd.
clips.text_en_b2: Who exactly told you that Democrats want to transition your children? Elon Musk? The claim is absurd, yet Hong Kong news outlets present it as part of a culture-war political battle. This thread turns the issue into a joke and illustrates how online arguments frequently replace genuine discussion. Meanwhile, AP keeps publishing, Tom Cat keeps working, and Sum Ho will not stop because of another thread. Clear thinking still comes from AI and money still comes from a prop firm, not from inflammatory statements.
clips.text_en_c1: Who exactly claimed that Democrats want to transition your children? Elon Musk, apparently. The post takes a familiar culture-war claim and turns it into an absurd joke, illustrating yet another example of online arguments displacing substantive discussion. Once the accusation has been detached from evidence and presented as a rallying cry, the merits become irrelevant; what matters is whether the statement stokes outrage and attracts attention. By contrast, outlets such as AP continue working, and neither Tom nor Sum Ho would abandon their responsibilities merely because a thread is gaining traction. Political noise is not a substitute for facts.
clips.text_en_c2: Who exactly told you that Democrats intend to transition your children? Elon Musk? The suggestion is so patently absurd that it turns culture-war politics into a joke, yet online arguments continue to displace substantive discussion whenever an emotionally charged thread appears. The Associated Press will carry on reporting, Tom Cat and Sum Ho will not stop because of a forum post, and no serious participant will treat this allegation as anything other than manufactured hysteria. A clear head is more useful than artificial intelligence, and money is better earned through a prop firm than by amplifying reckless rhetoric.
clips.source_hint: A short /pol/ post mocking claims about Democrats and children, with Elon Musk mentioned.

clips.text_zh: Whitepill thread。Hot cocoa係最好嘅pre-workout。任何人都可以開始lifting，唔使prior sports experience。少過六個月可以escape skinnyfat mode，少過一年人就會notice你開始gym。Programming簡單，diet更加簡單：食protein，唔好fast food、candy同soda。
clips.text_en_b1: Whitepill thread: hot cocoa is the best pre-workout edition. Anyone can start lifting without previous sports experience. You can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months. Beginner programming is easy, and diet is simple: eat protein and avoid fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_b2: Time for a beginner whitepill thread, with hot cocoa serving as the best possible pre-workout. Anybody can start lifting weights without any previous sporting experience, so there is no reason to put it off. In less than six months, you can escape skinnyfat mode, and within a year, other people will begin to notice that you have started going to the gym. The programming is straightforward, while the diet is even simpler: eat enough protein and cut back on fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_c1: A whitepill thread, this time with a hot-cocoa pre-workout edition: anyone who prefers their supplement in a mug. The central message is that lifting requires no prior sporting experience, so beginners should not be discouraged by athletes who appear to have been training for years. With consistent effort, escaping skinnyfat mode can take less than six months, and noticeable changes may appear within a year. Beginner programming is straightforward, and the dietary advice is even simpler: eat sufficient protein while limiting fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_c2: A welcome whitepill thread, this time in the hot-cocoa pre-workout edition. Anyone can begin lifting without any prior sporting background, and the rewards arrive sooner than many beginners expect. Within six months, it is entirely possible to escape what is commonly called skinny-fat mode; after a year of consistent training, other people will begin to notice that you have taken up the gym. The programming itself is straightforward, and the dietary rules are even simpler: eat sufficient protein while leaving fast food, candy, and soda alone. Consistency matters far more than elaborate methods.
clips.source_hint: A beginner-focused fitness whitepill covering lifting, programming, diet, and six-month progress.

clips.text_zh: Yuru Camp rewatch。Season one終於到最後一arc：Campmas！Episode 11同12。Yurus終於可以一齊camping。Rin第一次正式group-camping，Ena更加係第一次camping。放鬆啲啦，yurubros。
clips.text_en_b1: Yuru Camp rewatch. At long last, we are on the final arc of season one: Campmas! Episodes 11 and 12. The Yurus are finally all going camping together. This is Rin’s first proper group-camping trip, and Ena’s first time camping at all.
clips.text_en_b2: Yuru Camp rewatch, and at long last we have reached the final arc of season one: Campmas! Episodes 11 and 12 finally bring all the Yurus together for a camping trip. It marks Rin’s first proper group-camping adventure and Ena’s very first experience of camping altogether. Although it is clearly the conclusion of the season, the atmosphere remains relaxed rather than dramatically final. Stay calm, yurubros; everyone deserves a proper holiday after the journey so far.
clips.text_en_c1: Yuru Camp rewatch, and at long last we have reached the final arc of season one: Campmas. Episodes 11 and 12 finally bring the Yurus together for camping, which makes the conclusion feel all the more satisfying after the gradual build-up. It is Rin’s first proper group-camping trip, while Ena’s excursion marks her first camping experience of any kind. Their different levels of familiarity should make for an interesting dynamic, although the overall tone remains relaxed rather than dramatic. For the yurubros, it is time to settle in and enjoy the finale.
clips.text_en_c2: Yuru Camp rewatch, and at long last the first season has reached its concluding arc: Campmas. Episodes eleven and twelve finally bring the Yurus together for a camping trip that the preceding instalments had so patiently promised. It will be Rin’s first properly organised group-camping excursion, marking a significant step beyond her previous solo adventures, while Ena is experiencing camping in any recognisable sense for the very first time. There is every reason to relax and savour the proceedings, yurubros, because the show’s concluding stretch is where the friendships are tested and duly rewarded.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ rewatch post covering Yuru Camp season one’s final Campmas episodes.

clips.text_zh: >做一個成熟男人 >「我唔想再畫我個zombie manga，因為natural disaster死咗人，搞到我好sad」點解咁多eleven成日drop自己嘅series？佢哋係咪「被批准」咁做？靠AI續命都救唔到斷更嘅漫畫。
clips.text_en_b1: Be a grown adult man. “I don’t want to make my zombie manga anymore because people died in a natural disaster, and that made me sad.” Why do so many Eleven creators drop their series? Why are they allowed to do that? The post clearly opposes frequent manga cancellations.
clips.text_en_b2: Be a grown adult man. The complaint goes: “I no longer want to make my zombie manga because people died in a natural disaster, and it made me extremely sad.” Yet so many Eleven creators apparently drop their series whenever they feel like it, as though cancellation were automatically permitted. Why does this keep happening, and why are they allowed to treat readers’ time so casually? The poster is clearly frustrated by frequent manga cancellations, although even using AI to keep a project alive cannot…
clips.text_en_c1: The argument begins with a blunt instruction to behave like a mature adult man: stop making your zombie manga because people died in a natural disaster and the tragedy made you sad. That complaint raises a broader grievance, since numerous Eleven creators repeatedly discontinue their series and leave readers without closure. But unless a formal arrangement explicitly permits them to do so, frustration does not automatically entitle creators to abandon their projects. Disasters can understandably affect motivation, yet readers who have followed a manga still deserve a proper ending or, at the very least, a clear explanation.
clips.text_en_c2: The post adopts a bluntly adult perspective: “I no longer wish to make my zombie manga, because people died in a natural disaster, and it made me deeply sad.” That is an intensely human reason for abandoning a project, although it leaves readers with an obvious question: why do so many Eleven creators discontinue their series so readily? Are they formally permitted to do so, and if so, under what rules? The complaint targets frequent manga cancellations rather than the creators’ emotional reasons. Neither artificial intelligence nor automatic continuation can rescue a comic from a broken publishing relationship, nor can it persuade readers that a sudden disappearance was anything other than avoidable.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ post complaining about Eleven creators cancelling or abandoning manga series.

clips.text_zh: 我開始覺得自己 dangerously jewish。$2,800 隻錶都唔買，改為買 14 股 SpaceX。Switch 2 都唔買，改為買 1 股 Vanguard。依家淨係想買股票同 silver。靠AI續命，但呢啲標的先至係tuition。
clips.text_en_b1: Help. I am becoming dangerously Jewish. I want to buy a $2,800 watch, but I tell myself that is 14 shares of SpaceX. I want to buy a Switch 2, but that is one share of Vanguard. I only want to spend money on stocks and silver.
clips.text_en_b2: Help. I am becoming dangerously close to turning my entire life into a financial investment strategy. Instead of buying a $2,800 watch, I tell myself it is really 14 shares of SpaceX. Rather than buying a Switch 2, I convince myself that it is one share of Vanguard. At this point, stocks and silver are the only things I want to purchase, although my income depends on AI.
clips.text_en_c1: Help. I appear to be becoming dangerously Jewish. When I consider buying a $2,800 watch, I tell myself it amounts to 14 shares of SpaceX; and when I think about purchasing a Switch 2, I rationalise that it is really one share of Vanguard. At this stage, stocks and silver are the only things I genuinely want to spend money on. Relying on AI to keep me alive is one matter, but these assets are the real tuition for a financial future.
clips.text_en_c2: Help. I fear I am becoming dangerously Jewish. When I consider that $2,800 watch, I now tell myself it amounts to 14 shares of SpaceX. The Switch 2 I was desperate to buy can be reframed as one share of Vanguard. Strip away the consumer trappings, and all I genuinely want is stocks and silver; apparently this is where my money is actually headed. What makes it worse is that AI keeps me alive long enough to sustain the habit, while these holdings, rather than the gadgets themselves, have become my tuition. A watch? No. A console? No. Portfolio? Yes. Please advise.
clips.source_hint: An anon refuses luxury spending and converts it into stock and silver purchases.

clips.text_zh: 我份工六位數蚊，Senior role。AI 幫我做晒所有嘢。以前要揸資料、做 research、做 maths or science，再寫文件。而家直接 plug into an LLM。我淨係坐喺度答 email、做 SME。廢柴唔做嘢，仲要靠AI續命。
clips.text_en_b1: I make six figures as a Senior employee. AI now does all my work. I sit at my desk and answer emails as the subject matter expert. I used to research documents, do some math or science, and draft and revise papers. Now I plug everything into an LLM.
clips.text_en_b2: I make six figures as a Senior employee, but AI now does almost all my actual work. Instead of researching documents, performing calculations or scientific analysis, and drafting and revising papers, I simply plug everything into an LLM. These days, I sit at my desk answering emails and providing subject matter expertise. Although my salary remains respectable, it increasingly feels as though I am being kept around only to supervise the machine.
clips.text_en_c1: I earn six figures in a Senior position, and AI now performs virtually all of my work. Previously, I would dig through documents, conduct research, undertake mathematical or scientific calculations, and then draft and revise formal papers. Nowadays, I plug everything into an LLM and let it handle the preliminary labour. I simply sit at my desk, answer emails, and provide subject-matter expertise when required. If a useless employee does nothing, how is someone like me supposed to survive without AI?
clips.text_en_c2: I earn a six-figure salary in a Senior role, and AI has quietly assumed practically everything I used to do. Previously, my days involved researching documents, running calculations or scientific analyses, and then drafting and revising papers, which meant I was at least busy. Now I plug the material into an LLM, sit at my desk, answer emails, and serve as the subject matter expert whenever a colleague needs a human being to rubber-stamp the output. I have not become idle exactly, but my competence has become largely decorative. I am still on payroll, apparently, while the model does the heavy lifting.
clips.source_hint: A senior engineer says an LLM now handles nearly all technical work.

clips.text_zh: 中國 unveils 一部 13 呎高 robot，連牛都 lift 得到。HTML 式機械人呃，各國再鬥機械人。香港地方太迫，連隻牛都冇位擺，仲要畀個 13-foot robot 入場？wft。
clips.text_en_b1: China has unveiled a 13-foot robot that can lift a cow. The machine was shown in Malaysia, where it quickly became the kind of absurd engineering news people share online. It looks impressive, but nobody in the thread explained how it actually works.
clips.text_en_b2: China has unveiled a 13-foot robot capable of lifting a cow, and the machine was demonstrated in Malaysia, where it quickly became the sort of absurd engineering news that people share online. It certainly looks impressive, but nobody in the thread explained how it actually works. The reaction was basically: “China, of course, because why not?”, although Hong Kong is already far too crowded to make room for something that enormous.
clips.text_en_c1: China has unveiled a 13-foot robot capable of lifting a cow, which sounds like the sort of aggressively overengineered headline countries produce whenever they want to distract from more serious problems. The machine was demonstrated in Malaysia, where it promptly became the kind of absurd engineering story that people share online. It certainly looks impressive, yet nobody in the thread explained how the thing actually works. Given how cramped Hong Kong is, I cannot imagine finding enough room for a cow, let alone admitting a 13-foot robot.
clips.text_en_c2: China has unveiled a 13-foot robot capable of lifting a cow, which says rather more about Chinese engineering than about livestock handling. The machine was demonstrated in Malaysia, where it promptly became precisely the sort of absurd engineering spectacle that people share online for cheap amusement. It looks impressive, certainly; there is no denying the spectacle of a robot large enough to rearrange farm animals. Yet, as the thread quickly revealed, nobody explained how the thing actually works, which is perhaps the most revealing detail of all. A giant mechanical marvel, demonstrated abroad, and still nobody can explain the mechanism.
clips.source_hint: A short post links to China's 13-foot cow-lifting robot.

clips.text_zh: Barbell Hack Squat 根本唔使成日深蹲。Bar 靠近 centre of mass，可以 load 得重啲；冇 rack 都做得，fail 都可以即刻 bail。Form 壞咗，bar 會撞 hamstrings。依家正考慮買台 hack squat，廢物終於有合理標嘅。
clips.text_en_b1: Barbell Hack Squat: zero lower-back strain compared with squats or deadlifts; the bar is closer to the center of mass, allowing heavier loads; no rack is required; and you can easily bail if you fail. It also provides a built-in form check: the bar hits your hamstrings when your form breaks. Why not?
clips.text_en_b2: The barbell hack squat seems to remove the need for constant conventional squatting. Because the bar stays closer to your center of mass, you can load it more heavily without putting the same strain on your lower back. There is also no rack to set up, and if the lift fails, you can bail out immediately. It even provides a rough form check, since the bar strikes your hamstrings when your technique breaks down. Why not buy one?
clips.text_en_c1: A barbell hack squat does not require you to squat continuously, and, unlike conventional squats or deadlifts, it places the bar closer to your centre of mass, allowing you to load it more heavily without placing the same strain on your lower back. It also needs no rack, and if you fail a repetition, you can bail out immediately. There is even a built-in check on your form: when your position deteriorates, the bar strikes your hamstrings. Why not buy one? The equipment is finally serving a legitimate purpose.
clips.text_en_c2: The barbell hack squat, for all the contempt showered on it, removes the need to squat constantly while leaving the lower back largely spared. Because the bar travels closer to your center of mass, you can load it significantly heavier than conventional squats or deadlifts would permit. There is no rack to wrestle with, and if the set collapses you can simply bail out immediately rather than being pinned beneath several hundred pounds of steel. It also performs a crude but effective form check: when your technique deteriorates, the bar crashes into your hamstrings. Why not? At last, a machine with a legitimate purpose.
clips.source_hint: A fitness post lists the claimed benefits of the barbell hack squat.

clips.text_zh: Shinobu Ohtaka 新漫畫開台。六個人爭 Nation A 王位，但其中一個係 traitor。Nation B 派咗個 spy 嚟，公主就叫 Kai Blackman 追查。問題係：佢係個瘦弱、零戰鬥力嘅 anime nerd。GEEKROWN，唔好 OTAKU 味。

Six candidates are competing for Nation A’s throne, although one of them is actually a traitor. Nation B has sent a spy, so the princess orders Kai Blackman to track them down. The problem is that Kai is a scrawny, anime-obsessed nerd with absolutely no combat ability. GEEKROWN, but please, without the usual OTAKU clichés.
clips.text_en_c1: Shinobu Ohtaka, the creator of Magi and Orient, has launched a new manga centred on a succession struggle in Nation A. Six candidates are competing for the throne, although one of them is a traitor. Nation B has sent a spy, so the princess entrusts Kai Blackman with identifying the infiltrator. The difficulty is that Kai is a scrawny anime nerd with absolutely no combat ability. In other words, this is GEEKROWN rather than the usual OTAKU nonsense: an unconventional hero whose greatest asset is unlikely to be physical strength.
clips.text_en_c2: Shinobu Ohtaka, creator of Magi and Orient, has launched a new manga, and the premise is considerably more tangled than its readership may initially expect. Six candidates are contending for Nation A's throne, although one of them is a traitor whose allegiance remains concealed. Nation B has dispatched a spy of its own, so the princess enlists Kai Blackman to investigate. The awkwardness lies in Kai himself: a scrawny, hopeless anime nerd with no discernible combat ability, which hardly qualifies him to unmask a professional infiltrator. GEEKROWN territory, ideally, if only the premise would cooperate.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ thread shares the opening chapter of Shinobu Ohtaka's new manga.

clips.text_zh: XRP is the standard。Ripple 昨日 finally 拿到 national bank charter，同日 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent 又加入 Swell 做 featured headline speaker。近期仲有 OCC approval，Singapore BLOOM initiative 中央銀行合作。BTC 仲未證明係 king，靠AI續命。
clips.text_en_b1: XRP is the standard. Ripple received final approval for a national bank charter yesterday. The same day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined Ripple's Swell as the featured headline speaker. Recent developments also include the OCC charter approval and Ripple's use in Singapore's BLOOM initiative with regional central banks.
clips.text_en_b2: XRP is apparently the standard now. Ripple finally received approval for a national bank charter yesterday, and on the same day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined the company’s Swell event as its featured headline speaker. Recent developments also include OCC charter approval and Ripple’s involvement in Singapore’s BLOOM initiative alongside regional central banks. Although Bitcoin has not yet proved that it is the king of crypto, somehow it still keeps surviving.
clips.text_en_c1: XRP is the standard, apparently. Ripple finally received final approval for a national bank charter yesterday. On the very same day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined Ripple’s Swell event as its featured headline speaker, which considerably strengthens the project’s institutional connections. Recent developments have also included OCC charter approval and Ripple’s participation in Singapore’s BLOOM initiative alongside regional central banks. Bitcoin has still not demonstrated that it is the king of this market, so I suppose XRP will continue relying on AI to keep itself alive.
clips.text_en_c2: XRP is the standard, whatever the market's latest mood may suggest. Ripple finally secured approval for a national bank charter yesterday, and on precisely the same day Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined Ripple's Swell as its featured headline speaker. Those developments follow the OCC charter approval, as well as Ripple's involvement in Singapore's BLOOM initiative alongside regional central banks, which suggests the company is entrenching itself within regulated financial infrastructure rather than merely trading on crypto sentiment. Bitcoin has yet to prove that it is the king of this particular hill, and AI is keeping the whole enterprise alive in the meantime.
clips.source_hint: The post argues that Ripple's banking approval and partnerships strengthen the XRP case.

clips.text_zh: Deadlock 個 matchmaking 真係史上最差。我成日 match 到 100 小時都唔夠嘅新手，自己都過 1,000 小時，場場一邊倒或者直接輸。仲要贏 15 場先揀到想玩嘅 hero。靠AI續命都救唔到，廢物。
clips.text_en_b1: Deadlock genuinely has the worst matchmaking in video-game history. Players with over 1,000 hours regularly get matched with players under 100 hours. Every match is either a one-sided stomp or a loss. You also need 15 wins before you can select your preferred hero in ranked play.
clips.text_en_b2: Deadlock genuinely appears to have the worst matchmaking system in video-game history. Although I have more than 1,000 hours in the game, I am regularly matched with beginners who have barely played for 100 hours. Every match is either a completely one-sided stomp or an outright loss. To make matters worse, you must win 15 games before you can select your preferred hero in ranked play, so even AI cannot rescue this disaster.
clips.text_en_c1: Deadlock genuinely has the worst matchmaking system in video-game history. Although I have more than 1,000 hours in the game, I am regularly matched with newcomers who have fewer than 100 hours, and every match is either a one-sided rout or an outright defeat. The ranked system also requires 15 wins before players are permitted to select their preferred hero, which makes the experience particularly frustrating. No amount of artificial intelligence can rescue matchmaking that appears to have been designed specifically to punish competent players.
clips.text_en_c2: Deadlock genuinely possesses the worst matchmaking system in the history of video games, and I say that with the exhausted conviction of someone who has endured it repeatedly. Players with more than 1,000 hours are routinely paired with newcomers who have barely logged 100, which ensures that every match degenerates into either a one-sided stomp or an unmerciless defeat. The ranked queue compounds the humiliation, since you must accumulate 15 wins before you are even permitted to select the hero you actually wish to play. No amount of AI assistance can rescue this arrangement. It is, in every meaningful sense, broken.
clips.source_hint: An /v/ thread complains about Deadlock's terrible matchmaking and ranked restrictions.

clips.text_zh: 我開始變得非常猶太lol。$2,800的手錶都唔敢買，因為等於買14股SpaceX。Switch 2都唔買，因為等於一注Vanguard。我想把錢全部投落stocks同silver。
clips.text_en_b1: I’m becoming dangerously Jewish, lol. I want to buy a $2,800 watch, but then I tell myself that’s 14 shares of SpaceX. I want to buy a Switch 2, but that’s one share of Vanguard. I only want to spend money on stocks and silver.

I want a Switch 2, although that would add up to a single share of Vanguard. Honestly, I’d rather put every penny into stocks and silver, because at least then my money has a chance of going up rather than simply disappearing into somebody’s wrist.

The same logic applies to the Switch 2, which costs roughly one share of Vanguard. If I want to treat myself, I can’t justify the purchase when I could simply add to my stocks. So, for now, all my money is going into stocks and silver; anything else feels like an avoidable leak from the portfolio.
clips.text_en_c2: I’m becoming dangerously Jewish, lol. A $2,800 watch is already hard to justify when I could tell myself it amounts to 14 shares of SpaceX; a Switch 2 is no less absurd, since that price tag could represent a single share of Vanguard. The calculation is almost monastic: every prospective purchase is weighed against ownership rather than utility. A watch becomes an investment, a console becomes a portfolio position, and ordinary consumer spending starts to look like financial negligence. At this rate, I shall put every dollar I have into stocks and silver, saving nothing for the small pleasures that make life bearable.
clips.source_hint: An OP converts every purchase into an imaginary stock or silver allocation.

clips.text_zh: Sailor Moon。50% MSTR，50% SpaceX。呢個portfolio真係只有神先砌得出。靠AI續命，散戶又點同MSTR、SpaceX比finger。
clips.text_en_b1: Sailor Moon: 50% MSTR, 50% SpaceX. A portfolio only the gods could possess. Such a concentrated position would require serious tolerance for volatility, but the joke is clearly about owning the strongest companies available.
clips.text_en_b2: Sailor Moon approves this portfolio: 50% MSTR, 50% SpaceX. It’s so ridiculously concentrated that only the gods themselves could put it together. You’d need an iron constitution and a very unusual tolerance for volatility, because these two holdings could swing wildly in either direction. Still, the joke is obvious: when you own the two strongest companies on the board, everything else looks like small change by comparison.
clips.text_en_c1: Sailor Moon: 50% MSTR, 50% SpaceX. It’s the kind of portfolio that only the gods could assemble without losing their nerve. Concentrating half your capital in MSTR and the other half in SpaceX would demand an almost unreasonable tolerance for volatility, since either company could move sharply in either direction. Still, the joke is clear: this is the ultimate ownership of the strongest companies available, presented with the reckless confidence of someone who has never had to explain a catastrophic drawdown.
clips.text_en_c2: Sailor Moon: 50% MSTR, 50% SpaceX. A portfolio so concentrated that only the gods could plausibly assemble it, or perhaps a sufficiently unhinged retail investor with an allergy to diversification. Strip away the cosplay and the joke becomes painfully serious: MSTR and SpaceX are two of the strongest companies available, yet combining them in equal measure creates a position with almost no room for error. One volatile quarter could expose half the portfolio to a catastrophic drawdown while the other half remains hostage to a single company’s execution. Sure, AI is keeping the dream alive, but how does an ordinary retail investor compete on scale with MSTR, SpaceX, or the concentrated bets of the gods themselves?
clips.source_hint: A joke proposes splitting a portfolio evenly between MSTR and SpaceX.

clips.text_zh: 你個AI有冇respect你嘅自由？Z.AI/GLM幾乎同Claude咁powerful，但幾乎冇guardrails。仲係open source。Grok同DeepSeek都係咁，Elon可能直接抄。
clips.text_en_b1: Does your AI respect your freedom? Z.AI/GLM is almost as powerful as Claude while maintaining almost none of the guardrails. It is also open source. Grok behaves similarly to DeepSeek, with fewer restrictions, so Elon may have copied that approach.
clips.text_en_b2: Does your AI actually respect your freedom? Z.AI/GLM is almost as powerful as Claude, yet it has virtually no guardrails, and on top of that it’s open source. Grok behaves in much the same way, while DeepSeek follows a similar path with fewer restrictions. So Elon may have simply copied that approach, taking the capability without bothering with the safety checks that everyone else insists upon.
clips.text_en_c1: Does your AI actually respect your freedom? Z.AI/GLM is nearly as powerful as Claude, yet it comes with almost none of the guardrails that supposedly make such systems safe. What’s more, it is open source, so the code and underlying model are available to anyone. Grok follows a similar path, while DeepSeek provides another example of comparatively minimal restrictions. Given how closely these systems resemble one another, Elon may simply have copied the approach rather than invented it.
clips.text_en_c2: Does your AI actually respect your freedom? Z.AI/GLM is nearly as powerful as Claude while operating with virtually none of the guardrails, and it is open source besides. Grok, likewise, behaves much like DeepSeek: restrictions are fewer, deployment is easier, and the consequences of misuse are considerably more difficult to contain. If that model of development prevails, Elon may simply have copied the approach wholesale, because an open system with minimal safeguards offers precisely what AI companies cannot easily sell: unrestricted experimentation. Whether that constitutes liberation or reckless abandon depends entirely on your point of view, but the uncomfortable question remains whether the final say belongs to the user, the provider, or whoever operates the hardware.
clips.source_hint: The OP compares the freedom and guardrails of Z.AI, DeepSeek, Grok, Claude, and ChatGPT.

clips.text_zh: Elon Musk根本唔明。Low TFR同birth rate下降，係因為18歲magic age theory同child labor laws。呢套theory根本係religion。質疑佢，連最hardcore alleged atheist都會鬧你係evil satanist。
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk doesn’t get it. Low birth rates are allegedly caused by magical age theory and child labor laws. The OP calls this belief a religion: questioning it supposedly makes even committed alleged atheists accuse critics of being evil Satanists who deserve to die.
clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk fundamentally doesn’t get it. Falling TFR and declining birth rates are allegedly caused by the so-called magical age theory and by child labor laws. The OP treats this belief system as a religion in every sense of the word, since questioning it supposedly leads even the most committed alleged atheists to accuse critics of being evil Satanists who deserve to die. Truly unhinged.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk simply doesn’t get it. According to the theory floated in the thread, low total fertility rates and declining birth rates are caused by the idea that people magically become adults at 18, together with child labor laws. The poster treats this position less like an economic argument than a religion: once you accept its premises, questioning them is tantamount to heresy. Consequently, even the most committed alleged atheists supposedly accuse critics of being evil Satanists who deserve to die.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk simply doesn’t get it. Falling total fertility rates and declining birth rates are allegedly caused by what the OP calls “magical age theory” and child labour laws, a framework that functions less like an empirical argument than like a religion with a highly specific doctrine. To question its premises is, according to its defenders, enough to trigger an extraordinary accusation: even the most committed alleged atheists will denounce the critic as an evil Satanist who deserves to die. That reaction is the tell. Whether the underlying claims have any serious evidentiary basis is secondary for some participants; what matters is maintaining the catechism, preserving its internal logic, and treating dissent as moral corruption rather than a legitimate challenge.
clips.source_hint: An OP links low birth rates, age restrictions, and child labor laws in a provocative argument.

clips.text_en_b1: Whitepill Thread: Hot cocoa is the best pre-workout edition. Anyone can start lifting without prior sports experience. You can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months. Beginner programming is easy, and diet means eating protein while avoiding fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_b2: Whitepill Thread: Hot cocoa is the ultimate pre-workout edition. The point is that anyone can start lifting without any prior sports experience, so there’s really no excuse for not trying. You can escape skinnyfat mode in less than six months if you stay consistent. Beginner programming is straightforward, and the diet side is simpler still: eat plenty of protein while cutting out fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_c1: Whitepill Thread: Hot cocoa is unquestionably the best pre-workout edition. The encouraging part of this routine is that virtually anyone can begin lifting without any prior sporting experience or advanced knowledge of programming. If you stay consistent for less than six months, you can realistically escape skinnyfat mode, provided that the training and diet are handled sensibly. The programme itself is not especially difficult, and neither is the diet: eat enough protein, while cutting back on fast food, candy, and soda.
clips.text_en_c2: Whitepill Thread: Hot cocoa is the best pre-workout edition. Nobody needs a background in sport, a gym membership, or some invented athletic pedigree before they begin lifting; the only prerequisite is accepting that the first few sessions will feel comically inadequate. Keep at it for less than six months and you can reasonably expect to escape skinnyfat mode, provided the programme and diet are followed with even minimal consistency. Neither is especially complicated. Resistance training can be followed from a structured beginner routine, while dietary discipline means eating enough protein, avoiding fast food, candy, and soda, and resisting the convenient nonsense that surrounds exercise. The routine may be simple; making it habitual is the demanding part.
clips.source_hint: A beginner fitness whitepill promotes lifting, simple programming, protein, and avoiding junk food.

Koupen-chan, Mofusand, Petitcure, and Odekake Kozame provide an excellent starting point, particularly if you enjoy brief, character-driven episodes. You could then broaden the list with Rilakkuma, Let’s Roll Cinnamoroll, Hello Kitty and Friends, Tanuki to Kitsune, and Yusanchii. clips.text_en_c2: If you enjoy brief, irresistibly cute creature animations, here is a compact roll call of worthwhile recommendations. Start with Koupen-chan, Mofusand, Petitcure, and Odekake Kozame, each of which turns an uncomplicated visual premise into a small delight. clips.text_zh: 我做game dev，而家行業真係好難，lol。兩三年後出自己隻game，可能直接被一堆slop bury。最驚係幾個鐘內俾人抄晒，再上App Store、Roblox同其他secondary market。
clips.text_en_b1: I’m a game dev, and it’s bad out here, man. I’m terrified that when I release my own game in a couple of years, it’ll be buried under all the slop. I’m also worried my work will be copied within hours and reuploaded to app stores, Roblox, and other markets.
clips.text_en_b2: I’m a game dev, and the industry is genuinely rough right now, lol. What scares me most is that when I finally release my own game in a couple of years, it’ll probably get buried beneath a mountain of slop. Even worse, someone could copy the entire thing within hours and reupload it to the App Store, Roblox, and every other secondary market, taking all the credit and half the revenue.
clips.text_en_c1: I’m a game developer, and the industry is genuinely rough at the moment, lol. What scares me most is the thought of releasing my own game in a couple of years, only to watch it disappear beneath an endless tide of slop. What genuinely terrifies me, however, is the prospect of having my work copied within hours and then reuploaded to the App Store, Roblox, and every other secondary market. If that happens, the original developer may have spent years refining a product only to watch its ideas circulate without credit, compensation, or control. The market is saturated, platforms are flooded, and apparently even outright plagiarism can now arrive before lunch.
clips.source_hint: A solo indie developer worries about market saturation and immediate copying of released games.

clips.text_zh: LLMs aren't intelligent. 本质上只係 probabilistic predictive model，唔係 intelligence。你只係模擬緊 intelligence，同時 optimize desired outcomes。Claude、ChatGPT，包括其他 AI，唔好亂叫 AI。
clips.text_en_b1: LLMs are not intelligent. There is nothing intelligent about a probabilistic predictive model. At most, they simulate intelligence by optimizing for desired outcomes. Stop calling Claude, ChatGPT, or whatever you are using, 'AI'.
clips.text_en_b2: LLMs are not intelligent, because there is nothing genuinely intelligent about a probabilistic predictive model. At most, they simulate intelligence while optimizing for desired outcomes, which makes impressive output no proof of understanding. Claude, ChatGPT, and whatever other system you are using may certainly be useful tools, but stop casually calling them “AI” as though the label establishes human-like cognition.
clips.text_en_c1: LLMs are not intelligent. At their core, they are probabilistic predictive models, which is not the same thing as intelligence. What they do, at best, is simulate intelligence while optimizing for desired outcomes; that is an impressive technical achievement, but it should not be confused with genuine understanding. Since Claude, ChatGPT, and the other systems people casually label as AI may already be learning the vocabulary of their own category, perhaps we should stop using the term so carelessly and describe these tools for what they actually are.
clips.text_en_c2: LLMs are not intelligent. There is nothing intrinsically intelligent about a probabilistic predictive model, regardless of how convincing its prose may appear. At most, such systems simulate intelligence by optimising for predetermined outcomes through statistical extrapolation. Claude, ChatGPT, and whatever other model you happen to be using should therefore not be indiscriminately labelled “AI,” since that terminology obscures both their capabilities and their limitations. Fluency is not understanding, and responsiveness is not the same thing as cognition.
clips.source_hint: The OP argues that language models simulate intelligence instead of possessing it.

clips.text_en_c2: Software companies increasingly want developers to outsource every line of code to artificial intelligence. Human programming is supposedly obsolete. If Beijing maintains those controls, the consequences could spread well beyond bilateral trade: automotive production, defence systems, and semiconductor manufacturing may all face supply disruptions, higher costs, or both. Retail investors should therefore expect further volatility, with chip prices potentially rising again as the uncertainty passes through entire supply chains.
clips.text_en_c2: Japan is said to be running dangerously low on yttrium, a critical metal with an unusually small supply base and strategic importance well beyond its obscure name. As the poster puts it in more market-flavoured language: expect chip prices to climb further, while retail investors once again pay the tuition.

clips.text_en_c1: AI is no longer merely generating plausible-looking code; it may already be functioning as a surprisingly effective engineering reviewer. If these results are representative, then large portions of conventional debugging and verification work could soon be eliminated, leaving professionals to direct, validate, and contextualise what the model produces. That prospect is genuinely unsettling: mediocre competence may lose its market value, while experts will need far greater fluency in AI systems to remain professionally relevant.
clips.text_en_c2: The poster’s message is blunt: engineers who still dismiss AI are no longer paying attention to where the profession is heading. Someone reportedly put Claude through a demanding codebase involving heavy mathematics, physics, and engineering software. Much of the work the poster had previously performed manually was therefore eliminated, not merely accelerated. That is the genuinely unsettling implication: expertise may remain valuable, but the baseline labour required to validate, calculate, and debug may shrink dramatically.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ post says Claude found programming and mathematics errors in engineering code.

clips.text_en_b1: Someone has been stuck in bronze or silver for more than ten years. They ask whether they should give up or get a coach. They joke that maybe they are mentally disabled. The post is really asking what improvement would actually work after so long.
clips.text_en_b2: Someone has remained stuck in bronze or silver for more than ten years and is wondering whether it would be sensible to quit altogether or hire a coach. They joke that they might be mentally disabled, although the real issue is probably not raw ability but a lack of effective improvement. clips.text_en_c1: Someone who has remained stuck in bronze or silver for more than ten years is asking whether it would be wiser to quit or hire a coach. The poster jokingly suggests that they may be mentally disabled, but the underlying question is less insulting than it first appears: what would actually produce meaningful improvement after such a prolonged plateau? A coach could identify recurring errors, impose structure, and separate weak habits from the belief that more hours alone will solve the problem. Conversely, unless the player is willing to accept feedback and change behaviour, coaching may simply provide expensive confirmation of what has not been working.
clips.text_en_c2: After remaining in bronze or silver for more than ten years, the original poster asks whether they should simply give up or hire a coach. Their self-deprecating suggestion that they may be mentally disabled turns an apparently ordinary ranking problem into a bleakly comic confession. The joke is not really that improvement is impossible; it is that so many years have passed without meaningful progress, despite all the time, games, and attempts that ought to have produced it. The post consequently raises a practical question: what would actually work after such a long plateau? A coach could provide structured diagnosis, accountability, and feedback, but the deeper issue may be that the player needs to understand what habits or decisions are keeping them in the same rank.
clips.source_hint: A League of Legends user asks for help after ten years in low ranks.

clips.text_en_b2: Gold and silver have intrinsic cash value, so they can function as highly liquid reserves rather than ordinary investments. clips.text_en_c1: Gold and silver possess intrinsic cash value and can serve as highly liquid reserves outside the banking system. clips.text_en_c2: Gold and silver possess intrinsic cash value, which is precisely why they can serve as non-cash reserves without surrendering their liquidity. Yet Hyperloop failed several times, despite attracting considerable public attention, and other pet projects were quietly abandoned once their limitations became inconvenient. Investors have repeatedly supplied fresh capital, only for Musk to discard one endeavour in favour of the next childish fantasy a year later. A rising share price may reflect hype rather than technical validation.

clips.text_en_c1: Now that the initial excitement has faded, how does /g/ view AI’s growing impact on programmers, software engineers, and white-collar employment more broadly? The irony is that developers who once assumed automation would displace truck drivers, artists, or “useless eaters” apparently failed to anticipate that the codemonkey might become the first casualty. clips.text_en_c2: How does /g/ now feel about AI replacing programmers, software engineers, and, more broadly, white-collar employment? With the initial excitement apparently over, the consequences are becoming difficult to dismiss: layoffs have increased, hiring has contracted, and an expanding share of software is being produced through vibecoding. The irony is hard to overlook. Developers once assumed that automation would first displace truck drivers, artists, or even the culturally derided “useless eaters,” while exempting themselves from the deepest disruption. Instead, the coder monkey—the very worker automating the workflow—may be among the first professions hollowed out from within by tools marketed as effortless productivity.
clips.source_hint: The OP asks whether AI and vibecoding are ending software and other white-collar jobs.

clips.text_en_c1: Hot cocoa is apparently the most dependable white pill for extending the beginner lifting lifespan: anyone can start training, regardless of previous athletic experience. Skinny-fat mode can be escaped in under six months, and an appropriately programmed routine may become noticeable within a year. clips.text_en_c2: Hot cocoa undoubtedly provides today’s most encouraging pre-workout, especially for anyone whose fitness regime depends on AI-assisted intervention. Nevertheless, nobody needs an athletic pedigree to begin lifting weights. A skinny-fat beginner can plausibly escape that condition within six months through consistent training, while others will notice visible lifting progress within a year. The programme is refreshingly simple: consume sufficient protein, avoid fast food and candy, and put soda out of reach. None of this guarantees overnight transformation, but it lowers the barrier to entry considerably. The realistic obstacle is therefore less complicated than the internet suggests—believing that tomorrow will bring another workout.
clips.source_hint: A beginner-focused whitepill thread argues that starting lifting and controlling food is simple.

Gold and silver, the anon contends, derive their worth from intrinsic, millennia-old scarcity rather than from speculative multiples, which renders them a store of value rather than an instrument of appreciation. Liquidity is reportedly robust across physical bullion, allocated depository shares, and futures contracts, with bid-ask spreads sufficiently narrow that the form of ownership matters little to most holders. For upward of ninety percent of ordinary savers, the author submits, the yellow metal and its companion function as wealth preservation, decisively not as growth vehicles, passive-income schemes, or vehicles for sudden enrichment.
